    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"1.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"\
      1.0      General\\n\\n\\n      1.1    Scope\\n\\n\\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements\
      \ of the Employer on Safety,\\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor /\
      \ sub-contractor and\\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\\\
      n\\n\\n      1.2     Definition / languages\\n\\n\\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual\
      \ (EQM) forms an essential part of\\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed\
      \ by BMRCL  for  the\\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\\n\\n\\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS\
      \ & ABBREVIATIONS\\n\\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including\
      \ water, air\\n                    and land and other living creatures.\\n\\n                b)      Environmental\
      \ Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\\n                       present in such concentration\
      \ as may be or tend to be injurious to\\n                      environment.\\n\\n                 c)     \
      \ Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\\n                      environmental\
      \ pollutant.\\n\\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity\
      \ that\\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of\
      \ the\\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\\n\\n                e)      Monitoring\
      \ is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\\n                       provide information\
      \ regarding the levels of pollutants released during\\n                         construction.\\n\\n      \
      \                 f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\\\
      n                      area within the limits of the work as shown on the Plans. Construction\\n         \
      \                   site  shall  also  include  staging, and  debris  disposal  areas  and\\n            \
      \             transportation routes to and from these areas.\\n                g)     Noise is any unwanted\
      \ sound disturbance of the environment around\\n                       the area of construction operations.\\\
      n\\n                h)      Decibel is a measure on a logarithmic scale of the magnitude of a\\n         \
      \                 particular quantity (such as sound pressure, sound power) with respect\\n              \
      \            to a standardized reference quantity.\\n\\n                           i)    A - weighted Noise\
      \ levels in Decibels (referenced to 20 micro-\\n                      Pascal) as measured with A-weighting\
      \ network of standard\\n                    sound level meter,\\n                      abbreviated dB (A).\\\
      n\\n                         j)      Energy Equivalent Level (Leq) is the level of a steady noise\\n     \
      \                which has the same energy as the  fluctuating noise level\\n                        integrated\
      \  over  the  period  of  measurement.  Lmax  is  the\\n                 maximum Noise Level during the period\
      \ of measurement. L10\\n                   and L90 is the percentile exceeding levels of sound which is\\\
      n                    exceeded 10% and 90% of the time of measurement.\\n\\n                 k)     Waste \
      \ is  unwanted  surplus  substances  arising  from  the\\n                         application of all construction\
      \ operations and any substance or\\n                            article which is required to be disposed.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"l)     Suspended Particulate Matter is abbreviated\
      \ as SPM and\\n                           measured in µg/m3.\\n\\n                    m)     Environmental\
      \ Quality Management Manual is abbreviated as\\n                        EQM.\\n\\n                       \
      \    n)     Air Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as AMCP.\\n\\n                          o)    \
      \ Noise Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as NMCP.\\n\\n                           q)      Ministry\
      \ of Environment and Forests, Government of India is\\n                                abbreviated as MOEF.\\\
      n\\n                                   r)     Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi is abbreviated as\\\
      n                        CPCB.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"ENVIRONMENTAL\
      \ MANAGEMENT PLAN OUTLINE\\n\\n                 (Refer Environmental Protection Requirements, Appendix III)\\\
      n\\n           1.        CONTRACTOR’S OBLIGATION\\n          1.1           Contractor Details(including sub-contractors)\\\
      n          1.2          Organizational Chart (including sub-contractors).\\n          1.3         Persons\
      \ responsible for environmental matters, level of authority.\\n          1.4          Environmental lines\
      \ of communications.\\n           2.        PRESENTATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT APPROACH\\n         \
      \ 2.1         General\\n          2.1.1        Environmental Policy Statement of the Contractor\\n       \
      \   2.1.2       Methods of promoting environmental awareness.\\n          2.1.3         Specific  procedures\
      \   for   achieving   the   environmental  performance\\n                      requirements\\n          2.2\
      \           Air\\n          2.2.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.2.2         Corrective Action\\\
      n          2.2.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.2.3          Mitigation Schedule\\n          2.2.4\
      \        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Air Monitoring and Control Plan)\\n       \
      \   2.3         Water\\n          2.3.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.3.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.3.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.3.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.3.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Spill Prevention and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.4         Noise\\n          2.4.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.4.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.4.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.4.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.4.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Noise Monitoring and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.5        Waste\\n          2.5.1        Procedures for disposal of waste\\n          2.5.2  \
      \       Corrective Action\\n          2.5.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.5.3          Mitigation\
      \ Schedule\\n          2.5.4        Hazardous Wastes and Chemicals\\n          2.5.4.1       License Requirements\\\
      n          2.5.4.2       Storage\\n          2.5.4.3       Handling Procedure\\n                A similar\
      \ approach  will need to be adopted for the presentation of\\n                      procedures and provisions\
      \ to be followed to manage the construction\\n                      process as it relates to:\\n\\n\\n   \
      \                          Landscape Preservation;\\n                              Archaeological and Historical\
      \ Resources; etc\\n\\n          2.6         Environmental Emergency Procedures\\n                   Emergency\
      \  procedures  for  dealing  with  unforeseen  environment\\n                          situations not covered\
      \ by the specific requirements and provisions of\\n                       the Environmental Management Plan.\\\
      n\\n          2.7         General House Keeping\\n\\n          3.         ENVIRONMENTAL RECORDS\\n       \
      \                 Including monitoring, inspection and reporting.\\n\\n1.3.1      In this document\\n\\n \
      \               i)    The use of ‘shall’ indicates a mandatory requirement.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 11,\n      \"text\": \"ii)   The use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended.\\n\\\
      n                                     iii)   The use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered.\\\
      n\\n                          iv)   ‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment.\\n\\n                    \
      \  v)    Employer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC)\\n\\n                          vi) \
      \   Chief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall\\n                         responsible\
      \ for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document.\\n\\n                             vii)  BOCWA\
      \ means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions\
      \ of Service) Act, 1996\\n\\n                               viii)  BOCWR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998\\\
      n\\n                          ix)  DG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India.\\n\\n\
      \                      x)  BOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare\\n             \
      \        Cess Act, 1996\\n\\n                          xi)  BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ workers welfare\\n\\n                    Cess rules 1998\\n\\n                             xii)   Building\
      \ and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and\\n                         Condition of service)\
      \ Karnataka rules, 2006.\\n\\n                               xiii)  Notifications (Central and state) – collection\
      \ of cess.\\n\\n\\n          1.4      Application of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.4.1     This document\
      \ applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including\\n                            all aspects\
      \ conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be\\n                no activity associated\
      \ to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this\\n                  document.\\n\\n\\n     \
      \     1.5     Purpose of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.5.1    The objective of these guidelines is to\
      \ ensure that adequate precautions are\\n                   taken  to avoid  accidents, occupational  illness\
      \ and harmful  effects on  the\\n                  environment during construction.\\n\\n\\n          1.5.2\
      \     This document:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Describes the SHE interfaces between Employer\
      \ and the Contractor.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Details the processes by which the contractor\
      \ shall manage SHE issues\\n                          while carrying out the work under the contract.\\n\\\
      n                                     iii)   Describes by reference, the practices and procedures as given\
      \ in the\\n                BMRC  Project  Safety,  Health & Environment manual  for  best SHE\\n         \
      \               performance.\\n\\n\\n          1.5.3    These requirements shall be read together with BMRC\
      \ Project SHE Manual,\\n             OHSAS 18001-1999 Occupational Health and Safety Management System\\n\
      \               and ISO 14001: 2004 Environmental Management Systems.  Definition of\\n                key\
      \ terms used in these requirements related to OHSAS 18001 and ISO\\n                14001 standards are found\
      \ in BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"      1.0      General\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

    traffic, and road users.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"1.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"\
      1.0      General\\n\\n\\n      1.1    Scope\\n\\n\\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements\
      \ of the Employer on Safety,\\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor /\
      \ sub-contractor and\\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\\\
      n\\n\\n      1.2     Definition / languages\\n\\n\\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual\
      \ (EQM) forms an essential part of\\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed\
      \ by BMRCL  for  the\\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\\n\\n\\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS\
      \ & ABBREVIATIONS\\n\\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including\
      \ water, air\\n                    and land and other living creatures.\\n\\n                b)      Environmental\
      \ Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\\n                       present in such concentration\
      \ as may be or tend to be injurious to\\n                      environment.\\n\\n                 c)     \
      \ Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\\n                      environmental\
      \ pollutant.\\n\\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity\
      \ that\\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of\
      \ the\\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\\n\\n                e)      Monitoring\
      \ is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\\n                       provide information\
      \ regarding the levels of pollutants released during\\n                         construction.\\n\\n      \
      \                 f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\\\
      n                      area within the limits of the work as shown on the Plans. Construction\\n         \
      \                   site  shall  also  include  staging, and  debris  disposal  areas  and\\n            \
      \             transportation routes to and from these areas.\\n                g)     Noise is any unwanted\
      \ sound disturbance of the environment around\\n                       the area of construction operations.\\\
      n\\n                h)      Decibel is a measure on a logarithmic scale of the magnitude of a\\n         \
      \                 particular quantity (such as sound pressure, sound power) with respect\\n              \
      \            to a standardized reference quantity.\\n\\n                           i)    A - weighted Noise\
      \ levels in Decibels (referenced to 20 micro-\\n                      Pascal) as measured with A-weighting\
      \ network of standard\\n                    sound level meter,\\n                      abbreviated dB (A).\\\
      n\\n                         j)      Energy Equivalent Level (Leq) is the level of a steady noise\\n     \
      \                which has the same energy as the  fluctuating noise level\\n                        integrated\
      \  over  the  period  of  measurement.  Lmax  is  the\\n                 maximum Noise Level during the period\
      \ of measurement. L10\\n                   and L90 is the percentile exceeding levels of sound which is\\\
      n                    exceeded 10% and 90% of the time of measurement.\\n\\n                 k)     Waste \
      \ is  unwanted  surplus  substances  arising  from  the\\n                         application of all construction\
      \ operations and any substance or\\n                            article which is required to be disposed.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"l)     Suspended Particulate Matter is abbreviated\
      \ as SPM and\\n                           measured in µg/m3.\\n\\n                    m)     Environmental\
      \ Quality Management Manual is abbreviated as\\n                        EQM.\\n\\n                       \
      \    n)     Air Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as AMCP.\\n\\n                          o)    \
      \ Noise Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as NMCP.\\n\\n                           q)      Ministry\
      \ of Environment and Forests, Government of India is\\n                                abbreviated as MOEF.\\\
      n\\n                                   r)     Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi is abbreviated as\\\
      n                        CPCB.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"ENVIRONMENTAL\
      \ MANAGEMENT PLAN OUTLINE\\n\\n                 (Refer Environmental Protection Requirements, Appendix III)\\\
      n\\n           1.        CONTRACTOR’S OBLIGATION\\n          1.1           Contractor Details(including sub-contractors)\\\
      n          1.2          Organizational Chart (including sub-contractors).\\n          1.3         Persons\
      \ responsible for environmental matters, level of authority.\\n          1.4          Environmental lines\
      \ of communications.\\n           2.        PRESENTATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT APPROACH\\n         \
      \ 2.1         General\\n          2.1.1        Environmental Policy Statement of the Contractor\\n       \
      \   2.1.2       Methods of promoting environmental awareness.\\n          2.1.3         Specific  procedures\
      \   for   achieving   the   environmental  performance\\n                      requirements\\n          2.2\
      \           Air\\n          2.2.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.2.2         Corrective Action\\\
      n          2.2.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.2.3          Mitigation Schedule\\n          2.2.4\
      \        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Air Monitoring and Control Plan)\\n       \
      \   2.3         Water\\n          2.3.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.3.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.3.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.3.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.3.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Spill Prevention and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.4         Noise\\n          2.4.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.4.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.4.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.4.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.4.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Noise Monitoring and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.5        Waste\\n          2.5.1        Procedures for disposal of waste\\n          2.5.2  \
      \       Corrective Action\\n          2.5.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.5.3          Mitigation\
      \ Schedule\\n          2.5.4        Hazardous Wastes and Chemicals\\n          2.5.4.1       License Requirements\\\
      n          2.5.4.2       Storage\\n          2.5.4.3       Handling Procedure\\n                A similar\
      \ approach  will need to be adopted for the presentation of\\n                      procedures and provisions\
      \ to be followed to manage the construction\\n                      process as it relates to:\\n\\n\\n   \
      \                          Landscape Preservation;\\n                              Archaeological and Historical\
      \ Resources; etc\\n\\n          2.6         Environmental Emergency Procedures\\n                   Emergency\
      \  procedures  for  dealing  with  unforeseen  environment\\n                          situations not covered\
      \ by the specific requirements and provisions of\\n                       the Environmental Management Plan.\\\
      n\\n          2.7         General House Keeping\\n\\n          3.         ENVIRONMENTAL RECORDS\\n       \
      \                 Including monitoring, inspection and reporting.\\n\\n1.3.1      In this document\\n\\n \
      \               i)    The use of ‘shall’ indicates a mandatory requirement.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 11,\n      \"text\": \"ii)   The use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended.\\n\\\
      n                                     iii)   The use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered.\\\
      n\\n                          iv)   ‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment.\\n\\n                    \
      \  v)    Employer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC)\\n\\n                          vi) \
      \   Chief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall\\n                         responsible\
      \ for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document.\\n\\n                             vii)  BOCWA\
      \ means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions\
      \ of Service) Act, 1996\\n\\n                               viii)  BOCWR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998\\\
      n\\n                          ix)  DG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India.\\n\\n\
      \                      x)  BOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare\\n             \
      \        Cess Act, 1996\\n\\n                          xi)  BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ workers welfare\\n\\n                    Cess rules 1998\\n\\n                             xii)   Building\
      \ and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and\\n                         Condition of service)\
      \ Karnataka rules, 2006.\\n\\n                               xiii)  Notifications (Central and state) – collection\
      \ of cess.\\n\\n\\n          1.4      Application of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.4.1     This document\
      \ applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including\\n                            all aspects\
      \ conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be\\n                no activity associated\
      \ to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this\\n                  document.\\n\\n\\n     \
      \     1.5     Purpose of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.5.1    The objective of these guidelines is to\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"1.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"\
      1.0      General\\n\\n\\n      1.1    Scope\\n\\n\\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements\
      \ of the Employer on Safety,\\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor /\
      \ sub-contractor and\\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\\\
      n\\n\\n      1.2     Definition / languages\\n\\n\\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual\
      \ (EQM) forms an essential part of\\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed\
      \ by BMRCL  for  the\\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\\n\\n\\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS\
      \ & ABBREVIATIONS\\n\\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including\
      \ water, air\\n                    and land and other living creatures.\\n\\n                b)      Environmental\
      \ Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\\n                       present in such concentration\
      \ as may be or tend to be injurious to\\n                      environment.\\n\\n                 c)     \
      \ Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\\n                      environmental\
      \ pollutant.\\n\\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity\
      \ that\\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of\
      \ the\\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\\n\\n                e)      Monitoring\
      \ is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\\n                       provide information\
      \ regarding the levels of pollutants released during\\n                         construction.\\n\\n      \
      \                 f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\\\
      n                      area within the limits of the work as shown on the Plans. Construction\\n         \
      \                   site  shall  also  include  staging, and  debris  disposal  areas  and\\n            \
      \             transportation routes to and from these areas.\\n                g)     Noise is any unwanted\
      \ sound disturbance of the environment around\\n                       the area of construction operations.\\\
      n\\n                h)      Decibel is a measure on a logarithmic scale of the magnitude of a\\n         \
      \                 particular quantity (such as sound pressure, sound power) with respect\\n              \
      \            to a standardized reference quantity.\\n\\n                           i)    A - weighted Noise\
      \ levels in Decibels (referenced to 20 micro-\\n                      Pascal) as measured with A-weighting\
      \ network of standard\\n                    sound level meter,\\n                      abbreviated dB (A).\\\
      n\\n                         j)      Energy Equivalent Level (Leq) is the level of a steady noise\\n     \
      \                which has the same energy as the  fluctuating noise level\\n                        integrated\
      \  over  the  period  of  measurement.  Lmax  is  the\\n                 maximum Noise Level during the period\
      \ of measurement. L10\\n                   and L90 is the percentile exceeding levels of sound which is\\\
      n                    exceeded 10% and 90% of the time of measurement.\\n\\n                 k)     Waste \
      \ is  unwanted  surplus  substances  arising  from  the\\n                         application of all construction\
      \ operations and any substance or\\n                            article which is required to be disposed.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"l)     Suspended Particulate Matter is abbreviated\
      \ as SPM and\\n                           measured in µg/m3.\\n\\n                    m)     Environmental\
      \ Quality Management Manual is abbreviated as\\n                        EQM.\\n\\n                       \
      \    n)     Air Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as AMCP.\\n\\n                          o)    \
      \ Noise Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as NMCP.\\n\\n                           q)      Ministry\
      \ of Environment and Forests, Government of India is\\n                                abbreviated as MOEF.\\\
      n\\n                                   r)     Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi is abbreviated as\\\
      n                        CPCB.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"ENVIRONMENTAL\
      \ MANAGEMENT PLAN OUTLINE\\n\\n                 (Refer Environmental Protection Requirements, Appendix III)\\\
      n\\n           1.        CONTRACTOR’S OBLIGATION\\n          1.1           Contractor Details(including sub-contractors)\\\
      n          1.2          Organizational Chart (including sub-contractors).\\n          1.3         Persons\
      \ responsible for environmental matters, level of authority.\\n          1.4          Environmental lines\
      \ of communications.\\n           2.        PRESENTATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT APPROACH\\n         \
      \ 2.1         General\\n          2.1.1        Environmental Policy Statement of the Contractor\\n       \
      \   2.1.2       Methods of promoting environmental awareness.\\n          2.1.3         Specific  procedures\
      \   for   achieving   the   environmental  performance\\n                      requirements\\n          2.2\
      \           Air\\n          2.2.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.2.2         Corrective Action\\\
      n          2.2.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.2.3          Mitigation Schedule\\n          2.2.4\
      \        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Air Monitoring and Control Plan)\\n       \
      \   2.3         Water\\n          2.3.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.3.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.3.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.3.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.3.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Spill Prevention and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.4         Noise\\n          2.4.1          Mitigation Measures\\n          2.4.2         Corrective\
      \ Action\\n          2.4.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.4.4          Mitigation Schedule\\n   \
      \       2.4.5        Event Contingency Plan\\n                      Refer (Noise Monitoring and Control Plan)\\\
      n          2.5        Waste\\n          2.5.1        Procedures for disposal of waste\\n          2.5.2  \
      \       Corrective Action\\n          2.5.3         Preventive Action\\n          2.5.3          Mitigation\
      \ Schedule\\n          2.5.4        Hazardous Wastes and Chemicals\\n          2.5.4.1       License Requirements\\\
      n          2.5.4.2       Storage\\n          2.5.4.3       Handling Procedure\\n                A similar\
      \ approach  will need to be adopted for the presentation of\\n                      procedures and provisions\
      \ to be followed to manage the construction\\n                      process as it relates to:\\n\\n\\n   \
      \                          Landscape Preservation;\\n                              Archaeological and Historical\
      \ Resources; etc\\n\\n          2.6         Environmental Emergency Procedures\\n                   Emergency\
      \  procedures  for  dealing  with  unforeseen  environment\\n                          situations not covered\
      \ by the specific requirements and provisions of\\n                       the Environmental Management Plan.\\\
      n\\n          2.7         General House Keeping\\n\\n          3.         ENVIRONMENTAL RECORDS\\n       \
      \                 Including monitoring, inspection and reporting.\\n\\n1.3.1      In this document\\n\\n \
      \               i)    The use of ‘shall’ indicates a mandatory requirement.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 11,\n      \"text\": \"ii)   The use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended.\\n\\\
      n                                     iii)   The use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered.\\\
      n\\n                          iv)   ‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment.\\n\\n                    \
      \  v)    Employer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC)\\n\\n                          vi) \
      \   Chief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall\\n                         responsible\
      \ for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document.\\n\\n                             vii)  BOCWA\
      \ means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions\
      \ of Service) Act, 1996\\n\\n                               viii)  BOCWR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ Workers (Regulation of\\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998\\\
      n\\n                          ix)  DG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India.\\n\\n\
      \                      x)  BOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare\\n             \
      \        Cess Act, 1996\\n\\n                          xi)  BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction\
      \ workers welfare\\n\\n                    Cess rules 1998\\n\\n                             xii)   Building\
      \ and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and\\n                         Condition of service)\
      \ Karnataka rules, 2006.\\n\\n                               xiii)  Notifications (Central and state) – collection\
      \ of cess.\\n\\n\\n          1.4      Application of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.4.1     This document\
      \ applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including\\n                            all aspects\
      \ conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be\\n                no activity associated\
      \ to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this\\n                  document.\\n\\n\\n     \
      \     1.5     Purpose of this document\\n\\n\\n          1.5.1    The objective of these guidelines is to\
      \ ensure that adequate precautions are\\n                   taken  to avoid  accidents, occupational  illness\
      \ and harmful  effects on  the\\n                  environment during construction.\\n\\n\\n          1.5.2\
      \     This document:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Describes the SHE interfaces between Employer\
      \ and the Contractor.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Details the processes by which the contractor\
      \ shall manage SHE issues\\n                          while carrying out the work under the contract.\\n\\\
      n                                     iii)   Describes by reference, the practices and procedures as given\
      \ in the\\n                BMRC  Project  Safety,  Health & Environment manual  for  best SHE\\n         \
      \               performance.\\n\\n\\n          1.5.3    These requirements shall be read together with BMRC\
      \ Project SHE Manual,\\n             OHSAS 18001-1999 Occupational Health and Safety Management System\\n\
      \               and ISO 14001: 2004 Environmental Management Systems.  Definition of\\n                key\
      \ terms used in these requirements related to OHSAS 18001 and ISO\\n                14001 standards are found\
      \ in BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"      1.0      General\",\n  \"retained_lines\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\
      4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW\
      \ Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display\
      \ it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood\
      \ by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks\
      \ of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n                  submit a detailed\
      \ and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\\n\
      \         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following\
      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"3.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\
      3.0      Compliance\\n\\n3.1     Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)\\n\\n\\n3.1.1   A Memorandum of Understanding\
      \ placed at Appendix No.: 1 shall be executed after\\n          the award of contract before commencement\
      \ of work by the contractor with regard to\\n          various provisions on Safety, Health and Environment\
      \ to be practiced during the\\n          construction work.\\n\\n\\n3.2     BMRC’s SHE Policy and Management\
      \ Systems\\n\\n\\n3.2.1    The construction works shall be undertaken in accordance with BMRC’s SHE Policy\\\
      n        and Management Systems as amended from time to time provided in Project SHE\\n         Manual.\\\
      n\\n\\n3.3      Indian statutory requirements\\n\\n3.3.1     Primary statutory regulations\\n\\n\\n3.3.1.1\
      \  Contractor shall develop thorough understanding about Building and Other\\n        Construction Workers\
      \ (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act\\n        1996, Central Rules 1998, the building\
      \ & other construction workers welfare cess\\n        act 1996 and  central welfare rules 1998, Building and\
      \ Other Construction\\n       Workers [RE&C] Karnataka  Rules,  2006,  Building and Other Construction\\n\
      \       Workers Welfare Cess act 1996 and Central Rules 1998, Notification [Central &\\n         State] –\
      \ Collection of Cess, not only to satisfy the Inspectors’ perspective but the\\n       use  of  legislation\
      \  as  the  strong  tool  for  effective SHE management  at\\n        construction worksites. Contractor is\
      \ strongly advised to practice the principle\\n         of voluntary compliance.\\n\\n\\n 3.3.1.2 In order\
      \ to facilitate the contractor for better understanding on the various provisions of\\n         the above\
      \ Act and Rules, a tabulated information highlighting the Sections/Rules\\n          referring to the corresponding\
      \ registration of contractors, maintenance of registers and\\n         records, hours of work and wages, cess\
      \ & welfare, medical  facilities and safety\\n        requirements are given in Appendix No. 2. It is an indicative\
      \ one and not a limiting list.\\n\\n\\n3.3.2   In addition, the construction works shall be undertaken in\
      \ accordance with all applicable\\n         legislation and Indian statutory requirements listed below but\
      \ not limiting to:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Indian Electricity Act 2003 and Rules 1956\\n\\n       \
      \           ii)    National Building Code, 2005\\n\\n                  iii)    Factories Act, 1948, Delhi,\
      \ Uttarpradesh, Haryana Factories Rules.\\n\\n             iv)   Motor Vehicles Act as amended in 1994 and\
      \ The Central Motor Vehicles Rules,\\n              1989.\\n\\n           v)    Indian Road Congress Code\
      \ IRC: SP: 55-2001 ‘Guidelines on Safety In Road\\n               Construction Zones.\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   The Petroleum Act, 1934 and Rules 1976\\n\\n              vii)  Gas Cylinder Rules, 2003\\n\\n       \
      \        viii)   Indian Explosives Act. 1884, along with the Explosives substance Act 1908 and\\n        \
      \        the Explosives Rules 1983\\n\\n             ix)   The (Indian) Boilers Act, 1923\\n\\n          \
      \ x)   The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and Rules 1991\\n\\n             xi)   Minimum Wages Act, 1948\
      \ and Rules 1950\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"xii)   Contract Labour Act,\
      \ 1970 and Rules 1971\\n\\n                               xiii)   Child Labour (Prohibitions & Regulations)\
      \ Act, 1986 and Rules 1950\\n\\n                        xiv)  Environment Protection Act, 1986 and Rules 1986\\\
      n\\n                     xv)   Air (Prevention and control of Pollution) Act, 1981\\n\\n                 \
      \       xvi)  Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974\\n\\n                          xvii) \
      \ The Noise Pollution (Regulation & Control) Rules, 2000\\n\\n                           xviii)  Notification\
      \ on Control of Noise from Diesel Generator (DG) sets, 2002\\n\\n                       xix)  Recycled Plastic\
      \ Usage Rules, 1998\\n\\n                    xx)   Notification, Central Ground Water Board, Act January 1997\\\
      n\\n                       xxi)  Manufacture, Storage & Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules, 1989\\n\\n  \
      \                        xxii)  The Hazardous Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, 1989\\n\\n            \
      \               xxiii) Hazardous Waste Management Rules 1989 (as amended in 1999)\\n\\n                  \
      \    xxiv) Karnataka Preservation of Trees act, 1976 & rules, Batteries (Management and\\n               \
      \          Handling) Rules\\n\\n                    xxv)  Fly ash utilization notification, Sept 1999 as amended\
      \ in August 2003\\n\\n                      xxvi) Guidelines of Karnataka Urban Arts Commission\\n\\n    \
      \                    xxvii) Mysore Tramway Act.\\n\\n\\n          3.3.3    Workman Compensation Act, 1923\
      \ along with allied Rules\\n\\n\\n           3.3.3.1  The contractor shall ensure that all his employees /\
      \ workmen are covered under\\n               ‘Workmen Compensation Act’ and shall pay compensation to his\
      \ workmen as\\n               and when the eventuality for the same arises.\\n\\n\\n          3.3.4     Notwithstanding\
      \ the above Act/Rules, there  is nothing  in those  to exempt the\\n                     contractor from the\
      \ purview of any other Act or Rule in Republic of India for the safety\\n                      of men and\
      \ materials.\\n\\n\\n          3.3.5        If the requirements stated in this document are less stringent\
      \ than or in conflict with\\n                    the country’s applicable legislation, the latter shall apply.\\\
      n\\n\\n          3.4       International Standards, Guidelines & ISO Certifications\\n\\n\\n          3.4.1\
      \    The works should be undertaken in accordance with the applicable international\\n                   \
      \  guidelines, standards and specifications on SHE and every contract shall aim to\\n                   achieve\
      \ ISO certifications listed below during the currency of the contract:\\n\\n\\n             OHSAS 18001-1999\
      \   : Occupational Health and Safety Management System.\\n\\n                ISO 14001-2004         : Environmental\
      \ Management Systems.\\n\\n          3.4.2    The process of certification shall start immediately after the\
      \ award of the work and\\n                  complete within reasonable time. Towards this, the contractor\
      \ shall undertake the\\n                    required steps including appointment of ISO consultant for obtaining\
      \ the certification\\n                on  Occupational  Health  and  Safety  Management  System  and  Environment\\\
      n                Management System.\\n\\n\\n          3.4.3     In case of failure on the part of the contractor,\
      \ the Employer at the cost of the\\n                  contractor shall do the same.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\
      4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW\
      \ Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display\
      \ it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood\
      \ by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks\
      \ of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n                  submit a detailed\
      \ and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\\n\
      \         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following\
      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

  text: Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor must submit a detailed, comprehensive,
    contract-specific SHE Plan covering organizational arrangements, hazard identification, training, PPE, emergency
    procedures, and subcontractor safety compliance.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\
      4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW\
      \ Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display\
      \ it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood\
      \ by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks\
      \ of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n                  submit a detailed\
      \ and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\\n\
      \         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following\
      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

        quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\"\
          : \"4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of\
          \ the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively\
          \ and display it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other\
          \ languages understood by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n        \
          \  4.2       Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n \
          \                 submit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\
          \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and\
          \ regulations which, when implemented, will\\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions.\
          \ The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n           \
          \     i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n       \
          \           ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\\n        \
          \    management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\\n                Contractor’s\
          \ SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on \
          \ the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with\
          \  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s\
          \ policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for\
          \ addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient\
          \ information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\\\
          n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training\
          \ courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline\
          \ of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall\
          \ be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective equipment;\\n\\n    \
          \           viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\\n        \
          \        Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n                condition\
          \ and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and\
          \ procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety\
          \ plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\\\
          n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
          \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
          n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n       \
          \  Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed,\
          \ comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial\
          \ health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to\
          \ work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the\
          \ Employer in accordance with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the\
          \ SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification\
          \ to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the\
          \ Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor\
          \ shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5    \
          \ Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or\
          \ rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\n          without prejudice  to the\
          \ Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n           industrial health and environment\
          \ and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety\
          \  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\n4.6     The Contractor  shall\
          \ adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors\
          \ of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and\
          \ comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan\
          \ are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          4.0      Contractor\

        quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\"\
          : \"4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of\
          \ the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively\
          \ and display it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other\
          \ languages understood by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n        \
          \  4.2       Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n \
          \                 submit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\
          \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and\
          \ regulations which, when implemented, will\\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions.\
          \ The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n           \
          \     i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n       \
          \           ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\\n        \
          \    management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\\n                Contractor’s\
          \ SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on \
          \ the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with\
          \  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s\
          \ policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for\
          \ addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient\
          \ information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\\\
          n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training\
          \ courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline\
          \ of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall\
          \ be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective equipment;\\n\\n    \
          \           viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\\n        \
          \        Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n                condition\
          \ and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and\
          \ procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety\
          \ plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\\\
          n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
          \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
          n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n       \
          \  Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed,\
          \ comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial\
          \ health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to\
          \ work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the\
          \ Employer in accordance with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the\
          \ SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification\
          \ to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the\
          \ Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor\
          \ shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5    \
          \ Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or\
          \ rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\n          without prejudice  to the\
          \ Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n           industrial health and environment\
          \ and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety\
          \  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\n4.6     The Contractor  shall\
          \ adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors\
          \ of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and\
          \ comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan\
          \ are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          4.0      Contractor\
