        quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\"\
          : \"4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of\
          \ the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively\
          \ and display it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other\
          \ languages understood by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n        \
          \  4.2       Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n \
          \                 submit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\
          \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and\
          \ regulations which, when implemented, will\\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions.\
          \ The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n           \
          \     i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n       \
          \           ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\\n        \
          \    management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\\n                Contractor’s\
          \ SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on \
          \ the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with\
          \  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s\
          \ policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for\
          \ addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient\
          \ information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\\\
          n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training\
          \ courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline\
          \ of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall\
          \ be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective equipment;\\n\\n    \
          \           viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\\n        \
          \        Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n                condition\
          \ and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and\
          \ procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety\
          \ plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\\\
          n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
          \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
          n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n       \
          \  Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed,\
          \ comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial\
          \ health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to\
          \ work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the\
          \ Employer in accordance with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the\
          \ SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification\
          \ to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the\
          \ Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor\
          \ shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5    \
          \ Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or\
          \ rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\n          without prejudice  to the\
          \ Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n           industrial health and environment\
          \ and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety\
          \  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\n4.6     The Contractor  shall\
          \ adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors\
          \ of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and\
          \ comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan\
          \ are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          4.0      Contractor\

  text: The Contractor must execute an MOU regarding SHE practices (Appendix 1) after award and before work commencement,
    adhere to BMRCL's SHE Policy, comply with primary statutory regulations like the BOCW Act 1996 and Central Rules
    1998, and aim for OHSAS 18001-1999 and ISO 14001-2004 certifications.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"3.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\
      3.0      Compliance\\n\\n3.1     Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)\\n\\n\\n3.1.1   A Memorandum of Understanding\
      \ placed at Appendix No.: 1 shall be executed after\\n          the award of contract before commencement\
      \ of work by the contractor with regard to\\n          various provisions on Safety, Health and Environment\
      \ to be practiced during the\\n          construction work.\\n\\n\\n3.2     BMRC’s SHE Policy and Management\
      \ Systems\\n\\n\\n3.2.1    The construction works shall be undertaken in accordance with BMRC’s SHE Policy\\\
      n        and Management Systems as amended from time to time provided in Project SHE\\n         Manual.\\\
      n\\n\\n3.3      Indian statutory requirements\\n\\n3.3.1     Primary statutory regulations\\n\\n\\n3.3.1.1\
      \  Contractor shall develop thorough understanding about Building and Other\\n        Construction Workers\
      \ (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act\\n        1996, Central Rules 1998, the building\
      \ & other construction workers welfare cess\\n        act 1996 and  central welfare rules 1998, Building and\
      \ Other Construction\\n       Workers [RE&C] Karnataka  Rules,  2006,  Building and Other Construction\\n\
      \       Workers Welfare Cess act 1996 and Central Rules 1998, Notification [Central &\\n         State] –\
      \ Collection of Cess, not only to satisfy the Inspectors’ perspective but the\\n       use  of  legislation\
      \  as  the  strong  tool  for  effective SHE management  at\\n        construction worksites. Contractor is\
      \ strongly advised to practice the principle\\n         of voluntary compliance.\\n\\n\\n 3.3.1.2 In order\
      \ to facilitate the contractor for better understanding on the various provisions of\\n         the above\
      \ Act and Rules, a tabulated information highlighting the Sections/Rules\\n          referring to the corresponding\
      \ registration of contractors, maintenance of registers and\\n         records, hours of work and wages, cess\
      \ & welfare, medical  facilities and safety\\n        requirements are given in Appendix No. 2. It is an indicative\
      \ one and not a limiting list.\\n\\n\\n3.3.2   In addition, the construction works shall be undertaken in\

      \           ii)    National Building Code, 2005\\n\\n                  iii)    Factories Act, 1948, Delhi,\

      \ along with allied Rules\\n\\n\\n           3.3.3.1  The contractor shall ensure that all his employees /\
      \ workmen are covered under\\n               ‘Workmen Compensation Act’ and shall pay compensation to his\
      \ workmen as\\n               and when the eventuality for the same arises.\\n\\n\\n          3.3.4     Notwithstanding\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\
      5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk\
      \ to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle\
      \ or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public,\
      \ who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\\
      n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to\
      \ do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\\
      n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n\
      \                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\\
      n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n \
      \                  excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n \
      \               a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n        \
      \         However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                \
      \   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n         \
      \          purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n        \
      \              principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n \
      \                    or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\\
      n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n\
      \                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\\
      n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\\
      n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as\
      \ reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known\
      \ as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps\
      \ to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if\
      \ the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g.,\
      \ alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot\
      \ be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design\
      \ details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                            \
      \         iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n   \
      \                        protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should\
      \ measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g.,\
      \ use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing\
      \ itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design\
      \ work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\\
      n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\\
      n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\\
      n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n\
      \               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic\
      \ design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious\
      \ from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information.\
      \ The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions\
      \ for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner;\
      \ it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements.\
      \ The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved\
      \ and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1\
      \    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n          \
      \             etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n   \
      \                   to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions\
      \ shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles\
      \ made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc.\
      \ for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not\
      \ be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the\
      \ above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the gravity of\
      \ the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"5.0      Designer’s role\",\n  \"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"6.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"\
      6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1      Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor\
      \ shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\
      \ (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation\
      \ based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience\
      \ are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively\
      \ interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing\
      \  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare\
      \ Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct\
      \ and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored\
      \ by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\\n   \
      \      under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all\
      \ personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor\
      \ is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on\
      \ the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\\\
      n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address,\
      \ educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\n           of each personnel deployed\
      \ for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\\n          format prescribed for the purpose for\
      \ comments and approval well before the start of\\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these\
      \ personnel are authorised to work.\\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the\
      \ same shall be intimated\\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill\
      \ up the vacancy.\\n\\n\\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n6.4.1    For  all works carried\
      \ out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE\
      \ manpower lies with the main\\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\\\
      n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\\n        main contractor\
      \ to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions\
      \ shall be included in all sub-contract\\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n              \
      \    which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\\n                    \
      \  payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\\n                 \
      \  outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\\n                 \
      \         traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\\n\\n\\n          6.6    \
      \  Reporting of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE\
      \ Manager who shall report directly to\\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall\
      \ monitor adherence to this procedure\\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty\
      \ shall be levied as indicated in the\\n                    penalty clause.\\n\\n\\n          6.7      Inadequate\
      \ SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required\
      \ manpower as\\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up\
      \ vacancies\\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\\n \
      \                  contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\\n        \
      \              like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\\n          \
      \        the cost of contractor.\\n\\n\\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\\\
      n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\\n     \
      \             performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\\n          \
      \          Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\\n\\n\\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\\\
      n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\\n     \
      \               dispatch his duties effectively.\\n\\n\\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements\
      \ of such facilities / equipments to be provided\\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the\
      \ General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\
      5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk\
      \ to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle\
      \ or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public,\
      \ who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\\
      n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to\
      \ do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\\
      n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n\
      \                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\\
      n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n \
      \                  excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n \
      \               a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n        \
      \         However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                \
      \   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n         \
      \          purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n        \
      \              principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n \
      \                    or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\\
      n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n\
      \                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\\
      n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\\
      n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as\
      \ reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known\
      \ as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps\
      \ to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if\
      \ the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g.,\
      \ alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot\
      \ be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design\
      \ details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                            \
      \         iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n   \
      \                        protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should\
      \ measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g.,\
      \ use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing\
      \ itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design\
      \ work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\\
      n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\\
      n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\\
      n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n\
      \               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic\
      \ design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious\
      \ from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information.\
      \ The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions\
      \ for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner;\
      \ it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements.\
      \ The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved\
      \ and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1\
      \    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n          \
      \             etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n   \
      \                   to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions\
      \ shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles\
      \ made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc.\
      \ for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not\
      \ be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the\
      \ above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the gravity of\
      \ the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"5.0      Designer’s role\",\n  \"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\
      5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk\
      \ to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle\
      \ or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public,\
      \ who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\\
      n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to\
      \ do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\\
      n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n\
      \                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\\
      n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n \
      \                  excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n \
      \               a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n        \
      \         However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                \
      \   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n         \
      \          purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n        \
      \              principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n \
      \                    or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\\
      n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n\
      \                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\\
      n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\\
      n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as\
      \ reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known\
      \ as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps\
      \ to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if\
      \ the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g.,\
      \ alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot\
      \ be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design\
      \ details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                            \
      \         iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n   \
      \                        protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should\
      \ measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g.,\
      \ use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing\
      \ itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design\
      \ work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\\
      n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\\
      n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\\
      n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n\
      \               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic\
      \ design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious\
      \ from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information.\
      \ The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions\
      \ for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner;\
      \ it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements.\
      \ The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved\
      \ and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1\
      \    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n          \
      \             etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n   \
      \                   to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions\
      \ shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles\
      \ made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc.\
      \ for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not\
      \ be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\
      5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk\
      \ to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle\
      \ or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public,\
      \ who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\\
      n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to\
      \ do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\\
      n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n\
      \                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\\
      n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n \
      \                  excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n \
      \               a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n        \
      \         However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                \
      \   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n         \
      \          purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n        \
      \              principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n \
      \                    or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\\
      n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n\
      \                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\\
      n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\\
      n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as\
      \ reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known\
      \ as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps\
      \ to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if\
      \ the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g.,\
      \ alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot\
      \ be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design\
      \ details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                            \
      \         iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n   \
      \                        protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should\
      \ measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g.,\
      \ use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing\
      \ itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design\
      \ work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\\
      n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\\
      n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\\
      n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n\
      \               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic\
      \ design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious\
      \ from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information.\
      \ The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions\
      \ for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner;\
      \ it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements.\
      \ The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved\
      \ and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1\
      \    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n          \
      \             etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n   \
      \                   to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions\
      \ shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles\
      \ made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc.\
      \ for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not\
      \ be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the\
      \ above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the gravity of\
      \ the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"5.0      Designer’s role\",\n  \"\

      source_line_number\": 82,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 83,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"source_line_number\": 84,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"     \
      \     5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\"\n  \
      \  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"              \
      \ who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"                     structures and any\
      \ one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"                    affected by the work.\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n \
      \     \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"          5.2      General philosophy\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"          5.2.1    When considering\
      \ health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"                 what  is reasonable at the time\
      \ the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 15,\n      \"text\": \"                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to\
      \ be looked at during\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n     \
      \ \"text\": \"                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to\
      \ health and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \         excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"                a concern\
      \  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"                 However, a judgement has to be\
      \ made by weighing up one consideration against\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 21,\n      \"text\": \"                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but\
      \ also those of fitness for\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By \
      \ applying  these\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will\
      \ avoid\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \" \
      \                    or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 25,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \          considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 26,\n      \"text\": \"                    important\
      \ is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"                   proper exercise of judgement,\
      \ which takes account of health and safety issues.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 28,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 29,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"\
      text\": \"          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 32,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 33,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or\
      \ reduce risks by\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \          prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 36,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 37,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 38,\n      \"text\": \"                                 i)     consider\
      \  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 39,\n      \"text\": \"                        avoided (e.g., alter the\
      \ design to avoid the risk);\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 40,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"\
      text\": \"                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated\
      \ at source (e.g., ensure\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 42,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points\
      \ for lifting);\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \                                 iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the\
      \ risk that will\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                           protect all people;\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 46,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by\
      \ means of personal\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 48,\n      \"\
      text\": \"                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\"\n    },\n  \
      \  {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n  \
      \    \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 50,\n      \"text\": \"          5.4      Duty to provide\
      \ health and safety risks in the drawing itself\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 51,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"\
      text\": \"          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \        concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"                     detailed\
      \ information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"                   This information needs to be\
      \ included with the design to alert others to the risks,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"                  which they cannot reasonably be expected\
      \ to know. This is essential for the parties\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 58,\n      \"text\": \"               who have to use the design information.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design\
      \ assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 62,\n      \"text\": \"                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document,\
      \ the designer shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"\
      text\": \"                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication\
      \ of the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"           \
      \     need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                     specifications\
      \ or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"                be determined by the nature of\
      \ the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 69,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"          5.5      Employer’s approval\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 72,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining\
      \ structures\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \            to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n \

      \ conditions shall approve  all these\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 4,\n      \"text\": \"          designs.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\"\

      : \"5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\"\n    },\n\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"6.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"\
      6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1      Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor\
      \ shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\
      \ (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation\
      \ based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience\
      \ are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively\
      \ interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing\
      \  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare\
      \ Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct\
      \ and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored\
      \ by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\\n   \
      \      under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all\
      \ personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor\
      \ is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on\
      \ the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\\\
      n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address,\
      \ educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\n           of each personnel deployed\
      \ for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\\n          format prescribed for the purpose for\
      \ comments and approval well before the start of\\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these\
      \ personnel are authorised to work.\\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the\
      \ same shall be intimated\\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill\
      \ up the vacancy.\\n\\n\\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n6.4.1    For  all works carried\
      \ out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE\
      \ manpower lies with the main\\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\\\
      n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\\n        main contractor\
      \ to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions\
      \ shall be included in all sub-contract\\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n              \
      \    which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\\n                    \
      \  payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\\n                 \
      \  outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\\n                 \
      \         traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\\n\\n\\n          6.6    \
      \  Reporting of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE\
      \ Manager who shall report directly to\\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall\
      \ monitor adherence to this procedure\\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty\
      \ shall be levied as indicated in the\\n                    penalty clause.\\n\\n\\n          6.7      Inadequate\
      \ SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required\
      \ manpower as\\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up\
      \ vacancies\\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\\n \
      \                  contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\\n        \
      \              like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\\n          \
      \        the cost of contractor.\\n\\n\\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\\\
      n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\\n     \
      \             performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\\n          \
      \          Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\\n\\n\\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\\\
      n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\\n     \
      \               dispatch his duties effectively.\\n\\n\\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements\
      \ of such facilities / equipments to be provided\\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the\
      \ General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"6.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"\
      6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1      Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor\
      \ shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\
      \ (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation\
      \ based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience\
      \ are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively\
      \ interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing\
      \  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare\
      \ Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct\
      \ and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored\
      \ by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\\n   \
      \      under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all\
      \ personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor\
      \ is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on\
      \ the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\\\
      n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address,\
      \ educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\n           of each personnel deployed\
      \ for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\\n          format prescribed for the purpose for\
      \ comments and approval well before the start of\\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these\
      \ personnel are authorised to work.\\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the\
      \ same shall be intimated\\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill\
      \ up the vacancy.\\n\\n\\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n6.4.1    For  all works carried\
      \ out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE\
      \ manpower lies with the main\\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\\\
      n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\\n        main contractor\
      \ to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions\
      \ shall be included in all sub-contract\\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n              \
      \    which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\\n                    \
      \  payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\\n                 \
      \  outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\\n                 \
      \         traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\\n\\n\\n          6.6    \
      \  Reporting of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE\
      \ Manager who shall report directly to\\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall\
      \ monitor adherence to this procedure\\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty\
      \ shall be levied as indicated in the\\n                    penalty clause.\\n\\n\\n          6.7      Inadequate\
      \ SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required\
      \ manpower as\\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up\
      \ vacancies\\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\\n \
      \                  contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\\n        \
      \              like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\\n          \
      \        the cost of contractor.\\n\\n\\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\\\
      n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\\n     \
      \             performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\\n          \
      \          Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\\n\\n\\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\\\
      n\\n\\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\\\
      n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\\n     \
      \               dispatch his duties effectively.\\n\\n\\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements\
      \ of such facilities / equipments to be provided\\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the\
      \ General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\"\

    meetings chaired by the Project Manager with specified minimum members.

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\
