    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\

      \      \"text\": \"the  operation. The  training  shall cover the contents as given  in the General\\n   \

      \ are\\n        engaged for any work as per the format given in the General Instruction\\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/005\\\

  text: The Contractor must organize quality SHE training, behavioural-based training programs for executives, daily
    safety oaths for all employees and workmen, daily toolbox talks for high-risk workers, and refresher training
    every six months.
  evidence_ids:
  - J2d04a99a5037ea3a
  relation_type: none

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"9.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"\
      9.0     SHE Training\\n\\n\\n9.1     The behaviour of people at all levels of the contractor is critical for\
      \ SHE performance.\\n\\n\\n9.2     The contractor shall organise quality SHE training to engage Managers,\
      \ supervisors\\n        and other personnel in behavioural change and improve safety performance.\\n\\n\\\
      n9.3     The Contractor shall analyse the training requirements for  all the employees and\\n            \
      \ initiate a  training program  to demonstrate  that  all persons employed,  including\\n          subcontractors,\
      \ are suitably qualified, competent and fit. This will include:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Detailed Job\
      \  descriptions  for  all personnel,  to include  their  specific SHE\\n                  responsibilities\\\
      n\\n                  ii)    Specification of qualifications, competency and training requirements for  all\\\
      n               personnel\\n\\n                  iii)   Assessment and  recording  of  training needs  for\
      \  all  personnel,  including\\n                subcontractors’ employees in the workforce, vendor representatives\
      \ and site\\n                   visitors\\n\\n             iv)   A system for assessing new hirers e.g. previous\
      \ training\\n\\n           v)   A means of confirming that the system is effective\\n\\n             vi) \
      \  A matrix and schedule of training requirements, covering general, task–specific\\n             and SHE-related\
      \ training, showing the training frequency and interval between\\n                refresher courses\\n\\n\
      \              vii)   Timely, competent delivery of training courses\\n\\n\\n9.4     The contractor  shall\
      \ arrange behavioural-based  training programmes  for  all the\\n          executives to identify, recognise\
      \ and eliminate unsafe act and unsafe conditions.\\n\\n\\n9.5     The minimum Employer’s requirement of training\
      \ needs for various categories of\\n        employees are given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/006\\\
      n\\n\\n9.6     The contents of SHE training to Managers/Supervisors as given in general instruction\\n   \
      \    BMRC/SHE/CEO/007 shall be conducted.\\n\\n\\n9.7     The refresher-training programme to all employees\
      \ shall be conducted once in\\n          six months.\\n\\n\\n9.8      Toolbox talk as given in the Employer’s\
      \ Project SHE manual shall be conducted\\n          to all high-risk workmen everyday.\\n\\n\\n9.9      On-the\
      \ spot practical  skill development training on height safety including\\n         scaffold safety, crane\
      \ safety, welding safety, electrical safety, traffic safety for\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"marshals shall also be conducted to all foremen/ workmen who were associated\\n       \
      \            to the concerned jobs.\\n\\n\\n          9.10     Every employee including workman shall take\
      \ safety Oath daily without fail.\\n\\n\\n          9.11      All vehicle drivers including heavy vehicle\
      \ operators  shall be trained on\\n                  defensive driving at Central Training Institute KSRTC,\
      \ Shanthinagar Bangalore,\\n                  or any other driving institute registered under Motor Vehicles\
      \ Act.\\n\\n          9.12       All the above listed training programmes except at clause 9.11 shall be organised\
      \ by\\n                    the contractor only after taking approval from the Employer for the training faculty\
      \ /\\n                     organisation, content and durations.\\n\\n\\n          9.13      In case of failure\
      \ on the part of the contractor to provide  all the above-\\n                mentioned training programs to\
      \  all employees in time, the same shall be\\n                 provided by  the  Employer  through  accredited\
      \  agencies   if  required  by\\n                  formulating a common scheme to all contractors. Any administrative\
      \ expenses\\n               and training fee towards the same shall be at the cost of the contractor.\"\n\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"10.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\
      10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting\
      \ SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\\\
      n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\\n  \
      \               and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections\
      \ program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n \
      \                                   ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1  \
      \ Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined\
      \ intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the\
      \ Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program\
      \ are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee\
      \ Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors\
      \ (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                \
      \     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment\
      \ and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\\n\
      \                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                    Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and\
      \ equipment by operator\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding\
      \ supervisor\\n\\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools\
      \ by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary\
      \ electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances,\
      \ equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned\
      \ above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager\
      \ will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants,\
      \ equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators\
      \ and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed\
      \ on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections\
      \ for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules;\
      \ method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples\
      \ that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n             \
      \   i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork\
      \ before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor\
      \ shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\\
      n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n               \
      \ i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE\
      \ management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist\
      \ for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian\
      \ standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\\
      n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will\
      \ be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection\
      \ and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\"\n \
      \   }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          10.0    SHE Inspection\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"10.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\
      10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting\
      \ SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\\\
      n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\\n  \
      \               and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections\
      \ program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n \
      \                                   ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1  \
      \ Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined\
      \ intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the\
      \ Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program\
      \ are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee\
      \ Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors\
      \ (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                \
      \     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment\
      \ and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\\n\
      \                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                    Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and\
      \ equipment by operator\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding\
      \ supervisor\\n\\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools\
      \ by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary\
      \ electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances,\
      \ equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned\
      \ above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager\
      \ will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants,\
      \ equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators\
      \ and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed\
      \ on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections\
      \ for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules;\
      \ method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples\
      \ that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n             \
      \   i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork\
      \ before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor\
      \ shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\\
      n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n               \
      \ i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE\
      \ management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist\
      \ for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian\
      \ standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\\
      n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will\
      \ be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection\
      \ and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\"\n \
      \   }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          10.0    SHE Inspection\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"10.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\
      10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting\
      \ SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\\\
      n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\\n  \
      \               and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections\
      \ program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n \
      \                                   ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1  \
      \ Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined\
      \ intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the\
      \ Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program\
      \ are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee\
      \ Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors\
      \ (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                \
      \     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment\
      \ and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\\n\
      \                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                    Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and\
      \ equipment by operator\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding\
      \ supervisor\\n\\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools\
      \ by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary\
      \ electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances,\
      \ equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned\
      \ above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager\
      \ will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants,\
      \ equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators\
      \ and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed\
      \ on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections\
      \ for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules;\
      \ method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples\
      \ that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n             \
      \   i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork\
      \ before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor\
      \ shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\\
      n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n               \
      \ i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE\
      \ management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist\
      \ for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian\
      \ standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\\
      n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will\
      \ be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection\
      \ and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\"\n \
      \   }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          10.0    SHE Inspection\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"10.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\
      10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting\
      \ SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\\\
      n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\\n  \
      \               and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections\
      \ program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n \
      \                                   ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1  \
      \ Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined\
      \ intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the\
      \ Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program\
      \ are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee\
      \ Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors\
      \ (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                \
      \     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment\
      \ and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\\n\
      \                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                    Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and\
      \ equipment by operator\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding\
      \ supervisor\\n\\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools\
      \ by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary\
      \ electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances,\
      \ equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned\
      \ above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager\
      \ will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants,\
      \ equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators\
      \ and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed\
      \ on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections\
      \ for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules;\
      \ method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples\
      \ that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n             \
      \   i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork\
      \ before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor\
      \ shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\\
      n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n               \
      \ i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE\
      \ management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist\
      \ for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian\
      \ standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\\
      n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will\
      \ be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection\
      \ and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\"\n \
      \   }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          10.0    SHE Inspection\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"10.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\
      10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting\
      \ SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\\\
      n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\\n  \
      \               and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections\
      \ program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n \
      \                                   ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)\
      \    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1  \
      \ Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined\
      \ intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the\
      \ Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program\
      \ are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee\
      \ Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors\
      \ (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                \
      \     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment\
      \ and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\\n\
      \                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                    Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and\
      \ equipment by operator\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding\
      \ supervisor\\n\\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools\
      \ by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary\
      \ electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances,\
      \ equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned\
      \ above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager\
      \ will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants,\
      \ equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators\
      \ and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed\
      \ on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections\
      \ for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules;\
      \ method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples\
      \ that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n             \
      \   i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection\
      \ performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork\
      \ before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor\
      \ shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\\
      n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n               \
      \ i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE\
      \ management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist\
      \ for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian\
      \ standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\\
      n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will\
      \ be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection\
      \ and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\"\n \
      \   }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          10.0    SHE Inspection\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"11.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"\
      11.0    SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.1     General\\n\\n\\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess\
      \ potential risk, liabilities and the\\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental\
      \ plan and its\\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\\n\
      \           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\\n\\n\\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds\
      \ the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\\n          audit program during the construction\
      \ work.\\n\\n\\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\\n\\n\\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score\
      \ (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative\
      \ based on the pre-\\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\\\
      n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable\
      \ the Employer to\\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions\
      \ of Contract, the\\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE\
      \ Plan.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines. \
      \ The\\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\\\
      n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\\n      \
      \                invited to attend.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.4   Timing\\n\\n\\n                The Monthly\
      \ Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\\n                       prior to the scheduled\
      \ date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.1\
      \  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\\n                    \
      \    their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\\n                  \
      \  the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\\n                   \
      \ applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\\n                  achieved\
      \ by:\\n\\n\\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\\n\\n         \
      \                         Maximum Possible Score\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required\
      \ actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\\n                      classified as:\\n\\n\\\
      n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\\n           \
      \        No.\\n\\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within\
      \ 24\\n                                                          hours\\n\\n                 2    < 75%  \
      \ Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\\n                                Necessary\
      \               confirmed in writing to Employer\\n\\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable\
      \    Contractor rectification within one month\\n                                                    and confirmed\
      \ in writing to Employer\\n\\n\\n          11.2.6   Report\\n\\n              A copy of each Audit Report\
      \ will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed\
      \ in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective\
      \ actions are agreed upon.\\n\\n\\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\\n\\n\\n          11.3.1\
      \   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\\n                 \
      \   representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\\n           \
      \       submit the report to Employer.\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents\
      \ investigation findings and remedy\\n\\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation\
      \ and power requirements\\n\\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission\
      \ system in place\\n\\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the\
      \ current condition of power\\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\\\
      n\\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\\\
      n\\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\\\
      n\\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\\n\\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance\
      \ system and register.\\n\\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\\n\\n       \
      \      xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\\n\\n11.4   External SHE Audi\\n\\n\\n11.4.1    External\
      \ SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors\
      \ with the prior approval of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.1\
      \  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\\n         health/medical and\
      \ welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\\n        and control, traffic management, electrical\
      \ safety, rigging, safety of construction\\n        equipment and environment management.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.2\
      \  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\\n         standards. Audit report\
      \ shall also be presented as per the above formats.\\n\\n\\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted\
      \ on a quarterly basis throughout the\\n         currency of the contract.\\n\\n\\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE\
      \ Audit:\\n\\n\\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\\\
      n\\n\\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Organization\\n\\n                  ii)   \
      \ Communication and Motivation\\n\\n                  iii)   Time office\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection\\\
      n\\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\\n\\n             vi)   Budget allocation\\n\\n              vii)\
      \   Education and Training\\n\\n               viii)  Work permit system\\n\\n\\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\\n\\\
      n\\n                i)     Building and Structure\\n\\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\\\
      n\\n                  iii)    Material safety\\n\\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\\n\\n   \
      \        v)     Electrical system\\n\\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\\n\\n              vii)   Fire\
      \ prevention and control\\n\\n               viii)  Housekeeping\\n\\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery\
      \ safety\\n\\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\\n\\n             xi)   Welfare measures\\\
      n\\n              xii)   Environmental Management\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 25,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"11.4.5   Audit Documents:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents\
      \ available for the review by\\n                  the Audit team.\\n\\n\\n                               \
      \  i)   SHE policy\\n\\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\\n\\n                       \
      \              iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\\n\\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\\n\\n                          vi)   Accident\
      \ / near miss statistics and analysis\\n\\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records\
      \ for all personnel\\n\\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of\
      \ all equipments\\n\\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances\
      \ and gears\\n\\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\\n\\n              \
      \            xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\\n\\n                             xii)\
      \   Environmental management reports\\n\\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records\
      \ including mock drill\\n\\n\\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \      i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\\n           \
      \                interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\\n\\n                           \
      \         ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\\n      \
      \                     rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\\n\\n                                 \
      \    iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\\n         \
      \             gaps and weakness.\\n\\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility\
      \ for reaching a conclusion.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report\
      \ shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\\n                   conducting the\
      \ audit with a copy to the contractor.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\\n\\n\\n              \
      \                   i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\\\
      n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\\n   \
      \                     concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\\n\\n                   \
      \                 ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\\\
      n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\\\
      n                     and post-audit activities).\\n\\n                                     iii)    Principal\
      \ positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\\n                       observed\
      \ by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\\n                   may warrant\
      \ dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\\n                        achievement.\\n\\\
      n\\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists\
      \ shall be\\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\\\
      n\\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally\
      \ be\\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\\\
      n\\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with\
      \ a\\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\\\
      n                                    injury or business loss.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 26,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"11.4.9    Conformity Report & Action by Employer\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.1  The auditor shall inspect\
      \ the site after 14 days of conducting initial audit for checking\\n          the adequacy of implementation\
      \ of items maintained under priority 1 by the contractor\\n        and shall submit a conformity / non-conformity\
      \ report to the Employer with a copy to the\\n          contractor.\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.2  The auditor shall again\
      \ inspect after 28 days of conducting initial audit for checking the\\n        adequacy of implementation\
      \ of items mentioned under priority 2 by the contractor and\\n           shall submit a conformity / non-conformity\
      \ report to the Employer with a copy to the\\n          contractor.\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.3  In case of non-conformity\
      \ of items mentioned by auditor, the Employer shall take\\n         necessary steps including stoppage of\
      \ work and or imposing any penalty for getting the\\n          item implemented.\\n\\n\\n11.4.10   Failure\
      \ of contractor to conduct External SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.4.10.1 If the contractor fails to conduct the external\
      \ SHE audit in time, the Employer at\\n         the cost of contractor shall get it done.\"\n    }\n  ],\n\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"11.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"\
      11.0    SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.1     General\\n\\n\\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess\
      \ potential risk, liabilities and the\\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental\
      \ plan and its\\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\\n\
      \           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\\n\\n\\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds\
      \ the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\\n          audit program during the construction\
      \ work.\\n\\n\\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\\n\\n\\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score\
      \ (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative\
      \ based on the pre-\\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\\\
      n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable\
      \ the Employer to\\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions\
      \ of Contract, the\\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE\
      \ Plan.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines. \
      \ The\\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\\\
      n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\\n      \
      \                invited to attend.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.4   Timing\\n\\n\\n                The Monthly\
      \ Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\\n                       prior to the scheduled\
      \ date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.1\
      \  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\\n                    \
      \    their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\\n                  \
      \  the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\\n                   \
      \ applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\\n                  achieved\
      \ by:\\n\\n\\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\\n\\n         \
      \                         Maximum Possible Score\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required\
      \ actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\\n                      classified as:\\n\\n\\\
      n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\\n           \
      \        No.\\n\\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within\
      \ 24\\n                                                          hours\\n\\n                 2    < 75%  \
      \ Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\\n                                Necessary\
      \               confirmed in writing to Employer\\n\\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable\
      \    Contractor rectification within one month\\n                                                    and confirmed\
      \ in writing to Employer\\n\\n\\n          11.2.6   Report\\n\\n              A copy of each Audit Report\
      \ will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed\
      \ in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective\
      \ actions are agreed upon.\\n\\n\\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\\n\\n\\n          11.3.1\
      \   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\\n                 \
      \   representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\\n           \
      \       submit the report to Employer.\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents\
      \ investigation findings and remedy\\n\\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation\
      \ and power requirements\\n\\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission\
      \ system in place\\n\\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the\
      \ current condition of power\\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\\\
      n\\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\\\
      n\\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\\\
      n\\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\\n\\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance\
      \ system and register.\\n\\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\\n\\n       \
      \      xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\\n\\n11.4   External SHE Audi\\n\\n\\n11.4.1    External\
      \ SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors\
      \ with the prior approval of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.1\
      \  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\\n         health/medical and\
      \ welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\\n        and control, traffic management, electrical\
      \ safety, rigging, safety of construction\\n        equipment and environment management.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.2\
      \  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\\n         standards. Audit report\
      \ shall also be presented as per the above formats.\\n\\n\\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted\
      \ on a quarterly basis throughout the\\n         currency of the contract.\\n\\n\\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE\
      \ Audit:\\n\\n\\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\\\
      n\\n\\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Organization\\n\\n                  ii)   \
      \ Communication and Motivation\\n\\n                  iii)   Time office\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection\\\
      n\\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\\n\\n             vi)   Budget allocation\\n\\n              vii)\
      \   Education and Training\\n\\n               viii)  Work permit system\\n\\n\\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\\n\\\
      n\\n                i)     Building and Structure\\n\\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\\\
      n\\n                  iii)    Material safety\\n\\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\\n\\n   \
      \        v)     Electrical system\\n\\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\\n\\n              vii)   Fire\
      \ prevention and control\\n\\n               viii)  Housekeeping\\n\\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery\
      \ safety\\n\\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\\n\\n             xi)   Welfare measures\\\
      n\\n              xii)   Environmental Management\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 25,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"11.4.5   Audit Documents:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents\
      \ available for the review by\\n                  the Audit team.\\n\\n\\n                               \
      \  i)   SHE policy\\n\\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\\n\\n                       \
      \              iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\\n\\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\\n\\n                          vi)   Accident\
      \ / near miss statistics and analysis\\n\\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records\
      \ for all personnel\\n\\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of\
      \ all equipments\\n\\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances\
      \ and gears\\n\\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\\n\\n              \
      \            xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\\n\\n                             xii)\
      \   Environmental management reports\\n\\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records\
      \ including mock drill\\n\\n\\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\\n\\n\\n                           \
      \      i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\\n           \
      \                interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\\n\\n                           \
      \         ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\\n      \
      \                     rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\\n\\n                                 \
      \    iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\\n         \
      \             gaps and weakness.\\n\\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility\
      \ for reaching a conclusion.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report\
      \ shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\\n                   conducting the\
      \ audit with a copy to the contractor.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\\n\\n\\n              \
      \                   i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\\\
      n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\\n   \
      \                     concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\\n\\n                   \
      \                 ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\\\
      n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\\\
      n                     and post-audit activities).\\n\\n                                     iii)    Principal\
      \ positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\\n                       observed\
      \ by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\\n                   may warrant\
      \ dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\\n                        achievement.\\n\\\
      n\\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists\
      \ shall be\\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\\\
      n\\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally\
      \ be\\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\\\
      n\\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with\
      \ a\\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\\\
      n                                    injury or business loss.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 26,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"11.4.9    Conformity Report & Action by Employer\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.1  The auditor shall inspect\
      \ the site after 14 days of conducting initial audit for checking\\n          the adequacy of implementation\
      \ of items maintained under priority 1 by the contractor\\n        and shall submit a conformity / non-conformity\
      \ report to the Employer with a copy to the\\n          contractor.\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.2  The auditor shall again\
      \ inspect after 28 days of conducting initial audit for checking the\\n        adequacy of implementation\
