      source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which\
      \ result in death, serious injury or serious\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 24,\n      \"text\": \"               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find\
      \ out the cause of the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 25,\n    \
      \  \"text\": \"                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 26,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.1.3  Near misses\
      \ and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"                 soon as possible as they are\
      \ signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"                management system.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 33,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 36,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.2.1   It is\
      \ important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 37,\n      \"text\": \"                    the incident\
      \ is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 38,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 39,\n      \"text\": \"                     a)    take photographs and make\
      \ sketches\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"text\": \"        \
      \             b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 42,\n      \"text\": \"                    \
      \      conditions\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \                  c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"                     d)    consult expert\
      \ opinion where necessary\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 48,\n      \"\
      text\": \"                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 50,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.2.2  Having gathered\
      \ information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\":\
      \ 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"                     a)    establish the chain of events\
      \ leading to the accident or incident\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 54,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\"\n    },\n  \
      \  {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n  \
      \    \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"                      c)    consider\
      \ all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n      \"text\": \"                         the accident, and identify\
      \ the most probable cause The cause of an accident\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 59,\n      \"text\": \"                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific\
      \ act or omission that\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n    \
      \  \"text\": \"                      caused the accident must be identified.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up\
      \ action\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"          \
      \           a)    report on the findings and conclusions\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 67,\n      \"text\": \"                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\"\n\
      \    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"                   \
      \   c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 72,\n      \"text\": \"          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous\
      \ occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n     \
      \ \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"                      investigation. Contractor and his staff\
      \ shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 77,\n      \"text\": \"                  about the accident.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 79,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 80,\n      \"text\": \"          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of\
      \ accident till the Employer\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 81,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"                  completes the investigation.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 82,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 83,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 84,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 85,\n \
      \     \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"14.4.3\
      \     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"          the instructions without\
      \ delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"        be removed from the site immediately and  / or\
      \ punishable as per relevant penalty\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 7,\n      \"text\": \"          clause.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 8,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n   \
      \   \"text\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"title\": \"Accident\
      \ reporting and investigation\"\n}"

      ,\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                         \
      \                                 192\\n                     PART – I: SHE MANAGEMENT\\n\\n      1.0     \
      \ General\\n\\n\\n      1.1    Scope\\n\\n\\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements\
      \ of the Employer on Safety,\\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor /\
      \ sub-contractor and\\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\\\
      n\\n\\n      1.2     Definition / languages\\n\\n\\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual\
      \ (EQM) forms an essential part of\\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed\
      \ by BMRCL  for  the\\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\\n\\n\\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS\
      \ & ABBREVIATIONS\\n\\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including\
      \ water, air\\n                    and land and other living creatures.\\n\\n                b)      Environmental\
      \ Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\\n                       present in such concentration\
      \ as may be or tend to be injurious to\\n                      environment.\\n\\n                 c)     \
      \ Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\\n                      environmental\
      \ pollutant.\\n\\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity\
      \ that\\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of\
      \ the\\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\\n\\n                e)      Monitoring\
      \ is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\\n                       provide information\
      \ regarding the levels of pollutants released during\\n                         construction.\\n\\n      \
      \                 f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\\\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\
      4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW\
      \ Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display\
      \ it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood\
      \ by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks\
      \ of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n                  submit a detailed\
      \ and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\\n\
      \         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following\
      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"7.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\
      7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate\
      \  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees\
      \ and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase \
      \ the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation\
      \ and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n          7.2 \
      \     Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\\n\\n   \
      \                                 ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure\
      \  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                                     iii)   To review\
      \ SHE training\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"iv)   To review the contractor’s\
      \ monthly SHE report.\\n\\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in\
      \ building or other\\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\\n\\n          \
      \   vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\\n              \
      \  safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\\n               posters or\
      \ taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\\n\\n              vii)  To go round\
      \ the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\\n                detect unsafe  conditions\
      \ and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical\
      \ and welfare facilities.\\n\\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection\
      \ before every\\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\\n\\n           \
      \  ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\\n             and\
      \ maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\\n                construction\
      \ work\\n\\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\\\
      n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\\n       \
      \         construction work.\\n\\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling\
      \ different types of\\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest\
      \ remedial\\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\\n\\n              xii)  To review\
      \ the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\\n               persons/sub-contractors\
      \ for non-compliance if any.\\n\\n\\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall\
      \ be constituted and\\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and\
      \ employees\\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\\n\\n\\n7.4       Site SHE Committee\
      \ meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\\n        minimum members listed below:\\n\\\
      n         Chairman           Project Manager\\n\\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n  \
      \      Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                                        \
      \                   ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                                            \
      \                iii)  In charge of site electrics\\n                                           iv)  In charge\
      \ of stores.\\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different \
      \ sub\\n                                        functions.\\n                                           vi)\
      \  Sub – contractor’s representative\\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\\n    \
      \                                       ix)  Co-contractor representative.\\n                            \
      \        x)  SHE staffs\\n          Employer’s\\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\\\
      n          Representatives\\n\\n\\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least\
      \ once in a week with the\\n      minimum members listed below:\\n\\n    Chairman  Project Manager\\n\\n \
      \    Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\\n                 \
      \              ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\\n                               iii)  In-charge of\
      \ site electricity\\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\\\
      n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s\
      \ representative\\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\\n                          viii)\
      \  All SHE Staffs\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\\\
      n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\\
      n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\\
      n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\\
      n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2 \
      \   The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value\
      \ of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed\
      \ by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE\
      \ Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any\
      \ two SHE monthly\\n                  committee meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n      \
      \    7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n  \
      \               advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The\
      \ agenda should broadly cover the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation\
      \ of minutes\\n\\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance\
      \ / condition\\n\\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n      \
      \                    iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\\\
      n\\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\\n\\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’\
      \ SHE issues\\n\\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\\n\\n               \
      \                viii)  Report from Employer\\n\\n                          ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n  \
      \                    x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n     \
      \              No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n      \
      \              followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\\n      \
      \              the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary\
      \ Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the\
      \ meeting and\\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other\
      \ co/sub\\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of\
      \ monitory\\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that\
      \ the same\\n                          is implemented.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          7.0\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"15.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"\
      15.0    Emergency preparedness plan\\n\\n\\n15.1    The Contractor shall prepare as required under Rule 36\
      \ of BOCWR, an Emergency\\n        Response Plan for all work sites as a part of the Contractor SHE Plan.\
      \ The plan shall\\n          integrate the emergency response plans of the Contractor and all other subcontractors.\\\
      n        The Emergency Response Plan shall detail the Contractor’s procedures, including\\n          detailed\
      \ communications arrangements, for dealing with  all emergencies that could\\n           affect the  Site.\
      \   This include where applicable,  injury, sickness, evacuation,  fire,\\n         chemical spillage, severe\
      \ weather and rescue.\\n\\n\\n15.2    The contractor shall ensure that an Emergency Response Plan is prepared\
      \ to deal with\\n         emergencies arising out of:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Fire and explosion\\\
      n\\n                  ii)    Collapse of lifting appliances and transport equipment\\n\\n                \
      \  iii)    Collapse of building, sheds or structure etc.\\n\\n             iv)   Gas leakage or spillage of\
      \ dangerous goods or chemicals\\n\\n           v)   Bomb threatening, Criminal or Terrorist attack\\n\\n \
      \            vi)   Drowning of workers\\n\\n              vii)   Landslides getting workers buried floods,\
      \ Earthquake, storms and other natural\\n                 calamities.\\n\\n15.3     Arrangements shall be\
      \ made for emergency medical treatment and evacuation of the\\n           victim  in the event of an accident\
      \ or dangerous incident occurring, the chain of\\n       command and the responsible persons of the contractor\
      \ with their telephone numbers\\n        and  addresses  for  quick  communication  shall  be  adequately\
      \  publicized  and\\n         conspicuously displayed in the workplace.\\n\\n\\n15.4     Contractors shall\
      \ require to tie-up with the hospitals and fire stations located in the\\n         neighbourhood for attending\
      \ to the casualties promptly and emergency vehicle kept on\\n         standby duty during the working hours\
      \ for the purpose.\\n\\n\\n15.5      Contractor shall conduct an onsite emergency mock drill once in every\
      \ month for all his\\n         workers and his subcontractor’s workers.\\n\\n\\n15.6         It shall be the\
      \ responsibility of the contractor to keep the Local Law & Order Authorities\\n         informed and seek\
      \  urgent  help, as  the case may  be, so as  to  mitigate  the\\n        consequences  of an emergency. Prompt\
      \ communication  to BMRC, telephonically\\n             initially and followed by a written report, shall\
      \ be made by the contractor.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"15.0    Emergency preparedness plan\",\n\

      text\": \"15.1    The Contractor shall prepare as required under Rule 36 of BOCWR, an Emergency\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"        Response Plan\
      \ for all work sites as a part of the Contractor SHE Plan. The plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"          integrate the emergency response plans\
      \ of the Contractor and all other subcontractors.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 16,\n      \"text\": \"        The Emergency Response Plan shall detail the Contractor’s procedures, including\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"          detailed\
      \ communications arrangements, for dealing with  all emergencies that could\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"           affect the  Site.   This include where\
      \ applicable,  injury, sickness, evacuation,  fire,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 19,\n      \"text\": \"         chemical spillage, severe weather and rescue.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"15.2    The contractor shall ensure that an Emergency\
      \ Response Plan is prepared to deal with\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 23,\n      \"text\": \"         emergencies arising out of:\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 25,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 26,\n      \"text\": \"                i)     Fire and explosion\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"                  ii)    Collapse of lifting appliances and transport\
      \ equipment\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 29,\n      \"text\":\
      \ \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"    \
      \              iii)    Collapse of building, sheds or structure etc.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"             iv)   Gas leakage or spillage of dangerous\
      \ goods or chemicals\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 33,\n      \"\
      text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \           v)   Bomb threatening, Criminal or Terrorist attack\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n\
      \      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 36,\n      \"text\": \"             vi)   Drowning of workers\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 37,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 38,\n      \"text\": \"              vii)   Landslides getting workers\
      \ buried floods, Earthquake, storms and other natural\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 39,\n      \"text\": \"                 calamities.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"text\": \"15.3     Arrangements shall be made for emergency medical\
      \ treatment and evacuation of the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 42,\n      \"text\": \"           victim  in the event of an accident or dangerous incident occurring, the\
      \ chain of\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\": \"\
      \       command and the responsible persons of the contractor with their telephone numbers\"\n    },\n   \
      \ {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"        and  addresses\
      \  for  quick  communication  shall  be  adequately  publicized  and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"         conspicuously displayed in the workplace.\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n\
      \    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 48,\n      \"text\": \"15.4     Contractors shall\
      \ require to tie-up with the hospitals and fire stations located in the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"         neighbourhood for attending to the casualties\
      \ promptly and emergency vehicle kept on\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 50,\n      \"text\": \"         standby duty during the working hours for the purpose.\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"15.5      Contractor shall conduct an onsite emergency\
      \ mock drill once in every month for all his\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 54,\n      \"text\": \"         workers and his subcontractor’s workers.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\"\
      : 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n \
      \     \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\
      source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"15.6         It shall be the responsibility of the contractor\
      \ to keep the Local Law & Order Authorities\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\"\
      : 58,\n      \"text\": \"         informed and seek  urgent  help, as  the case may  be, so as  to  mitigate\
      \  the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"  \
      \      consequences  of an emergency. Prompt communication  to BMRC, telephonically\"\n    },\n    {\n   \
      \   \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"             initially and followed\
      \ by a written report, shall be made by the contractor.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"\

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\
      \    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 15,\n  \"review_status\": \"\
      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n199\\\
      n\\n          5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\\\
      n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\\n        \
      \             structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\\n      \
      \              affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\n\\n\\n          5.2.1\
      \    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\\n              \
      \   what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\n                  \
      \ hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n                  \
      \   detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\n               \
      \     safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n                \
      \   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n                a\
      \ concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n                 However,\
      \ a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                   another so the\
      \ cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n                   purpose,\
      \  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n                      principles,\
      \ it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n                     or reduce\
      \ risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\n                    considerations\
      \  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n                    important is the\
      \ approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\n                   proper exercise\
      \ of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk\
      \ Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or\
      \ reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control\
      \ or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include\
      \ the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented\
      \ from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid\
      \ the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should\
      \ be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design details of items to be lifted\
      \ include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                                     iii)     failing this,\
      \ priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n                           protect\
      \ all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk\
      \ by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\\\
      n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1\
      \      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\\n                  concluded\
      \ that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\n                     detailed information\
      \ shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\n                   This information needs\
      \ to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\n                  which they cannot reasonably\
      \ be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n               who have to use the design information.\\\
      n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health\
      \ and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\\\
      n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\\\
      n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n \
      \               need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n   \
      \                  specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\\\
      n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\\n\\\
      n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false\
      \ work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations\
      \ included in the method statements in addition\\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’\
      \ designer or  his approved proof check\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.        \
      \      September 2026     Section Page 11 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n    \
      \    50.15998077392578,\n        15.768376350402832,\n        564.21923828125,\n        24.210372924804688\n\

      : 8,\n      \"text\": \" \\ni) \\nconsider if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n201\\\
      n          6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage\
      \ SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n                  which case the effectiveness would be\
      \ lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\\n                      payroll of the main contractor only and\
      \ not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\\n                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This\
      \ condition does not apply to positions like\\n                          traffic marshals who are engaged\
      \ almost on a daily requirement basis.\\n\\n\\n          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\\\
      n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\\n\
      \                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\\\
      n                    penalty clause.\\n\\n\\n          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n        \
      \  6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\\n              \
      \       illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\\n              \
      \    created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\\n                   contractor’s\
      \ cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\\n                      like paper advertisement\
      \ or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\\n                  the cost of contractor.\\n\\n\\\
      n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\\n\\n\\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule\
      \ VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\\n                 do any work which  is\
      \ unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\\n                  performance  of the SHE  duties\
      \  for respective category mentioned  in General\\n                    Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\\n\\n\\\
      n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.9.1    As per schedule\
      \ VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\\n                 such  facilities,\
      \ equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\\n                    dispatch his duties\
      \ effectively.\\n\\n\\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements of such facilities / equipments\
      \ to be provided\\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\\n\\n\\n          7.1         All employees should be \
      \ able  to  participate  in the making and monitoring  of\\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial\
      \ health and environment at their place of work. The\\n                   establishment of site SHE committees\
      \ in which employees and Contractor and sub-\\n                     contractor  management  are  represented\
      \  can  increase  the  involvement  and\\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure\
      \ the formation and monitor the\\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\\n\\n\\n\
      \          7.2      Terms of Reference\\n\\n\\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee\
      \ shall be as follows;\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies\
      \ and practices\\n\\n                                    ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s\
      \ site SHE plan and ensure  its\\n                        implementation\\n\\n                           \
      \          iii)   To review SHE training\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.       \
      \       September 2026     Section Page 13 of 114\",\n  \"text_blocks\": [\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n   \

      \  515.8872680664062,\n        688.9717407226562\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"\
      6.5 \\nEmployment status of SHE personnel \\n \\n \\n6.5.1 \\nNo contractor shall engage SHE manpower from\
      \ any outsourcing agencies in \\nwhich case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on\
      \ the \\npayroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or \\noutsourcing\
      \ manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like \\ntraffic marshals who are engaged\
      \ almost on a daily requirement basis.  \\n \\n6.6  \\nReporting of SHE personnel \\n \\n6.6.1 \\nAll SHE\
      \ personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to \\nthe Chief Project Manager.\
      \ The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure \\nat all times. In case of non-adherence penalty\
      \ shall be levied as indicated in the \\npenalty clause. \\n \\n6.7 \\nInadequate SHE personnel \\n \\n6.7.1\
      \ \\n In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as \\nillustrated in General\
      \ Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies \\ncreated within 14 days, the same shall be provided\
      \ by the Employer at \\ncontractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same \\nlike\
      \ paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at \\nthe cost of contractor. \\n\
      \ \\n6.8 \\nProhibition of performance of other duties \\n \\n6.8.1 \\nAs per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE\
      \ personnel shall be required or permitted to \\ndo any work which is unconnected to, inconsistent with or\
      \ detrimental to the \\nperformance of the SHE duties for respective category mentioned in General \\nInformation\
      \ BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 \\n \\n6.9 \\nFacilities to be provided to SHE personnel \\n \\n6.9.1 \\nAs per schedule\
      \ VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with \\nsuch facilities, equipment and information\
      \ that are necessary to enable him to \\ndispatch his duties effectively. \\n \\n6.9.2 \\nThe minimum Employer’s\
      \ requirements of such facilities / equipments to be provided \\nfor SHE personnel are given in the General\
      \ Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003 \\n \\n7.0 \\nContractor SHE Committee \\n \\n7.1 \\nAll employees should be\
      \ able to participate in the making and monitoring of \\narrangements for safety, industrial health and environment\
      \ at their place of work. The \\nestablishment of site SHE committees in which employees and Contractor and\
      \ sub-\\ncontractor management are represented can increase the involvement and \\ncommitment of employees.\
      \ The contractor shall ensure the formation and monitor the \\nfunctioning of contractor SHE committees. \
      \ \\n \\n7.2 \\nTerms of Reference \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        85.5599594116211,\n  \

      : 4,\n      \"text\": \" \\n7.2.1 \\nThe Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows; \\n\"\n\

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        200\\n          consultants as applicable as per\
      \ the contract conditions shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures\
      \ like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many\
      \ times etc. for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards,\
      \ shall not be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If\
      \ any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the\
      \ gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\\n\\n\\n6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1    \
      \  Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed\
      \ in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n \
      \        requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum\
      \ educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\\
      n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n     \
      \    the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor\
      \ shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause\
      \ 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the\
      \ contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall\
      \ attract penalty as per details given\\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2\
      \    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned\
      \ to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person\
      \ whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove\
      \ that person from the site without any\\n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from\
      \ Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\\

      \ as per the contract conditions shall approve all these \\ndesigns. \\n \\n5.6 \\nAny non-standard structures\

      \ are not adhered penalty shall be imposed \\ndepending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\
      \ \\n \\n6.0 \\nContractor SHE Organisation \\n \\n6.1 \\nEducation and Experience \\n \\n6.1.1 \\nThe contractor\
      \ shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General \\nInstruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed\
      \ at the end) based upon the statutory \\nrequirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the\

      \ shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and \\nexperienced as per clause 6.1.1. \\\
      n \\n \\n \\n6.2 \\nConduct and Competency \\n6. 2.1 \\nThe conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE\

      \ and fill up the vacancy.  \\n \\n6.4 \\nResponsibility of SHE personnel \\n \\n6.4.1 \\nFor all works carried\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"4.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\
      4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\\n\\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW\
      \ Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display\
      \ it at conspicuous places at work sites\\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood\
      \ by the majority of construction\\n                   workers.\\n\\n\\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks\
      \ of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\\n                  submit a detailed\
      \ and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n\
      \      \"text\": \"include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\\n\
      \         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\\n          following\
      \ but not be restricted to:\\n\\n\\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation\
      \ and arrangements for SHE\\n\\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the\
      \ Contractor’s proposed\\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring\
      \ the\\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\\n\\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff\
      \ who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line\
      \  of  communication  with  the  proposed\\n                Contractor's agent;\\n\\n             iv)   A\
      \ statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\\n                estimating\
      \ hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\\n\\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated\
      \ for this Contract and sufficient information to\\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for\
      \ achieving effective and  efficient\\n                health and safety procedures;\\n\\n             vi)\
      \   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\\n\\n             be provided\
      \ by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\\n\\n              vii)   Details of\
      \ the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\\n                including personal protective\
      \ equipment;\\n\\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring\
      \ that\\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\\n     \
      \           condition and are operated in a safe manner;\\n\\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s\
      \ policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's\
      \ safety plan;\\n\\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to\
      \ SHE\\n                 related matters, and\\n\\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure\
      \ for reporting and investigating\\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\\\
      n\\n\\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\\n         Employer\
      \ to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\\n           detailed, comprehensive\
      \ and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\\n            site safety, industrial health and\
      \ environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any\
      \ and all submissions of supplements\\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance\
      \ with the agreed\\n         procedures.\\n\\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s\
      \ opinion, insufficient or requires\\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works\
      \ and the safety of all\\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\\\
      n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\\n          plan\
      \ to the Employer for review.\\n\\n\\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or\
      \ the Employer’s\\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\\\
      n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\\n        \
      \   industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\\n          contractor  to\
      \ adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\\n          execution of the Work.\\n\\n\\\
      n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\\n           practically\
      \ possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\\n           parties each have\
      \ a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\\n\\n\\n4.7     The details of contents to be\
      \ covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\\n         No.: 3.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\
