## Key Parameters and Source Statements

- SHE targets for the Works include achieving zero total recordable injuries, zero reportable environmental incidents, 100% personnel induction as per the approved SHE plan, total compliance with inspection/audit schedules, 100% incident recording/reporting, 100% PPE adherence, and executing work with least disturbance to the environment, traffic, and road users.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 2.0 — ‘SHE’ Targets and Goals|Clause 2.0 — ‘SHE’ Targets and Goals]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 11, 12; quotation `J89e4131252f66e20`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/1`.

- Contractual definitions establish that 'shall' indicates a mandatory requirement, 'should' indicates a strongly recommended guideline, and 'may' indicates a guideline to be considered.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 1.0 — General|Clause 1.0 — General]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 8, 9, 10, 11; quotation `Jde330d8fa6968654`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/0`.

- The SHE management requirements apply universally across all contractor scopes, subcontractors, and associated agencies with zero exemptions.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 1.0 — General|Clause 1.0 — General]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 8, 9, 10, 11; quotation `Jde330d8fa6968654`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/0`.

- The Contractor must formulate a SHE policy under Section 39 of the BOCW Act, get it approved by the DG, and display it conspicuously at work sites in Kannada, Hindi, and other languages understood by the majority of construction workers.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor must submit a detailed, comprehensive, contract-specific SHE Plan covering organizational arrangements, hazard identification, training, PPE, emergency procedures, and subcontractor safety compliance.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- If the Employer considers the SHE plan insufficient or requiring modification, the Contractor must submit a revised plan within 7 days of receiving instructions.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- The Contractor must execute an MOU regarding SHE practices (Appendix 1) after award and before work commencement, adhere to BMRCL's SHE Policy, comply with primary statutory regulations like the BOCW Act 1996 and Central Rules 1998, and aim for OHSAS 18001-1999 and ISO 14001-2004 certifications.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 3.0 — Compliance|Clause 3.0 — Compliance]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 12, 13; quotation `J7502791d30e9933d`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/2`.

- Designers must minimize health and safety risks for constructors, maintainers, cleaners, repairers, dismantlers, demolishers, and the general public by applying a hierarchy of risk control starting with hazard prevention, combating at source, collective protection, and personal protective equipment as a last resort.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role|Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 14, 15, 16; quotation `Jf8809a71af85b566`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/4`.

- All structures such as scaffolds, falsework, launching girders, and earth retaining structures must include design calculations in method statements and be approved by the Employer's designer or approved proof check consultants.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role|Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 14, 15, 16; quotation `Jf8809a71af85b566`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/4`.

- Non-standard structures like rebar trestles, very old, corroded, or repeatedly repaired structures lacking accurate national standard design calculations are strictly prohibited from site use even for short durations.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role|Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 14, 15, 16; quotation `Jf8809a71af85b566`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/4`.

- The main contractor bears sole responsibility for providing required SHE personnel across all works executed by the main contractor and all sub-contractors, and all SHE manpower must be on the direct payroll of the main contractor.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation|Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 16, 17; quotation `J9b89915bf84b73ea`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/5`.

- If the contractor fails to provide minimum required SHE manpower or fails to fill vacancies within 14 days, the Employer shall provide them at the contractor's cost including administrative expenses like paper advertisements and manpower consultant charges.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation|Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 16, 17; quotation `J9b89915bf84b73ea`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/5`.

- Monthly SHE committee meetings require a minimum period of 21 days between any two meetings, and meeting agendas must be circulated by the secretary at least 7 working days in advance.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.

- Construction SHE committee meetings must be conducted at least once a week, and meeting minutes must be prepared using Form SF-002 and sent to all members within 2 working days.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.

- All vehicle drivers and heavy vehicle operators must be trained on defensive driving at the Central Training Institute KSRTC, Shanthinagar, Bangalore, or another registered motor vehicles act driving institute.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 9.0 — SHE Training|Clause 9.0 — SHE Training]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 20, 21; quotation `J2d04a99a5037ea3a`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/8`.

- Planned general inspections include monthly site safety committee inspections, weekly safety inspections by construction supervisors, and daily safety inspections by the contractor site SHE team.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection|Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 21, 22; quotation `J146a1bdce2491605`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/9`.

- Routine inspections cover daily plant/equipment checks by operators, weekly scaffold inspections, monthly electrical hand tool checks, quarterly temporary electrical system checks, and half-yearly lifting machinery inspections by approved competent persons.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection|Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 21, 22; quotation `J146a1bdce2491605`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/9`.

- Specific inspections must be performed without predetermined dates on high-risk activities such as heavy lifting, confined space entry, welding/gas cutting, and formwork concreting.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection|Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 21, 22; quotation `J146a1bdce2491605`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/9`.

- Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) is weighed on a 1-10 scale and conducted at least 7 days prior to the scheduled Monthly SHE Committee meeting, classifying scores under 60% as immediate rectification within 24 hours, under 75% as rectification within 7 days, and under 90% as rectification within one month.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 11.0 — SHE Audit|Clause 11.0 — SHE Audit]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 22, 23, 24, 25, 26; quotation `Ja911fab00f3bad38`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/10`.

- External SHE audits are conducted quarterly throughout the currency of the contract, with audit reports sent to the Employer within 7 days, and conformity inspections scheduled after 14 days for Priority 1 items and 28 days for Priority 2 items.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 11.0 — SHE Audit|Clause 11.0 — SHE Audit]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 22, 23, 24, 25, 26; quotation `Ja911fab00f3bad38`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/10`.

- The contractor must submit daily reports of the total number of workmen engaged by all entities (including subcontractors) within 2 hours of starting any shift through tele-fax or email, under the primary duty of the Chief SHE Manager.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 13.0 — SHE Submittals to the Employer|Clause 13.0 — SHE Submittals to the Employer]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 26, 27; quotation `J8edcd48c6ac2acdf`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/12`.

- Monthly SHE reports containing 18 specified categories (including man-hours, accident details, training, audits, and PPE status) must be prepared and submitted in 3 copies within the 7th of the next month to the Employer.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 13.0 — SHE Submittals to the Employer|Clause 13.0 — SHE Submittals to the Employer]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 26, 27; quotation `J8edcd48c6ac2acdf`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/12`.

- All accidents and dangerous occurrences must be informed verbally immediately to the Employer, followed by written reports within 24 hours in the specified format.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 14.0 — Accident reporting and investigation|Clause 14.0 — Accident reporting and investigation]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 27, 28, 29, 30; quotation `J226b324d4a855c2e`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/13`.

- Statutory accident reporting under Rule 210 of BOCWR requires notice within 4 hours for fatal accidents and 72 hours for other reportable accidents sent to the Regional Labour Commissioner, beneficiary board, Director General, and next of kin.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 14.0 — Accident reporting and investigation|Clause 14.0 — Accident reporting and investigation]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 27, 28, 29, 30; quotation `J226b324d4a855c2e`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/13`.

- Contractors must formulate a SHE policy approved by the DG under Section 39 of the BOCW Act and display it prominently at worksites in Kannada, Hindi, and other languages understood by the majority of workers.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor must submit a detailed, contract-specific SHE Plan covering organization, hazard identification, training, PPE, equipment maintenance, subcontractor compliance, disciplinary procedures, and accident reporting.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- The Contractor must establish a site SHE Committee within 14 days of award of contract and communicate the notification via Form SF 001, conducting monthly meetings chaired by the Project Manager with a minimum of 21 days between consecutive monthly meetings.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.

- Construction SHE Committee meetings must be conducted at least once a week, and meeting agendas must be circulated by the Secretary at least seven working days in advance.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.

- Minutes of the SHE committee meeting must be prepared using Form SF 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days, preferably by mail or fax followed by a hardcopy, and displayed on notice boards.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.

- Contractors must prepare an Emergency Response Plan under Rule 36 of BOCWR as part of the Contractor SHE Plan, integrate subcontractor emergency plans, conduct monthly onsite emergency mock drills, tie up with neighborhood hospitals and fire stations, and keep emergency vehicles on standby.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 15.0 — Emergency preparedness plan|Clause 15.0 — Emergency preparedness plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 30; quotation `Je1056d4f95bb7c6f`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/14`.

- Contractors may utilize services of experts and agencies empanelled under Rule 250 of BOCWR or listed in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/010 for training, internal audit, and SHE services, subject to prior mandatory approval by the Employer.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 16.0 — Experts / Agencies for SHE services|Clause 16.0 — Experts / Agencies for SHE services]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 30; quotation `Jd9fbeda14a931cb7`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/15`.

- The SHE targets and goals for Tender Package P1 include zero total recordable injuries, zero reportable environmental incidents, 100% personnel induction as per approved SHE plans, 100% audit compliance, 100% incident reporting, 100% appropriate PPE adherence, and execution with least environmental and traffic disturbance.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 2.0 — ‘SHE’ Targets and Goals|Clause 2.0 — ‘SHE’ Targets and Goals]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 11, 12; quotation `J89e4131252f66e20`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/1`.

- The Contractor must submit a detailed contract-specific SHE plan within 4 weeks of receiving the notification of acceptance of the tender, and must revise and submit the plan within 7 days if instructed by the Employer.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 14; quotation `Ja0fd942c8ef785e3`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/6`.

- Designers must minimize risks to constructors, maintainers, cleaners, repairers, dismantlers, demolishers, and the public by applying a hierarchy of risk control: preventing hazards at design, combating at source, collective protection measures, and using personal protection only as a last resort.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 15; quotation `Jb9e46b4aa31bbb3d`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/7`.

- All SHE personnel must be on the direct payroll of the main contractor rather than subcontractors or outsourcing agencies, with the sole exception of daily-requirement personnel such as traffic marshals.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17; quotation `J24927d393ae56edd`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/9`.

- The Contractor must submit a detailed and comprehensive contract-specific SHE Plan within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 13, 14; quotation `J6e268122a6c15b66`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/3`.

- The contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee must be constituted within 14 days of the award of contract and communicate notification via Form SF 001.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 18; quotation `J5e54b356035ab68b`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/10`.

- Site SHE Committee meetings must be conducted at least once a month, while Construction SHE Committee meetings must be conducted at least once a week.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 18; quotation `J5e54b356035ab68b`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/10`.

- A minimum period of 21 days must be maintained between any two monthly SHE committee meetings, and meeting agendas must be circulated at least seven working days in advance.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 19; quotation `J1529db7f21b890ef`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/11`.

## Open Questions and Contradictions

- Source discrepancy: SHE 7.8.1 requires agenda circulation at least seven working days before the scheduled meeting, while Form SF/001 states at least two days. Preserve the different wording without selecting precedence. Monthly Site SHE Committee meetings under 7.4 and weekly Construction SHE Committee meetings under 7.5 are distinct source provisions.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee|Clause 7.0 — Contractor SHE Committee]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 17, 18, 19; quotation `J9eeb4ca708ebff86`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/6`.
  - Evidence: [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_appendices_instructions_forms#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Appendices, General Instructions and Forms|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Appendices, General Instructions and Forms]]; `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`; PDF page(s) 116; quotation `J6af8ef325f51b6bf`. JSON: `parsed_json/vol3/forms/she_committee_forms.json#/forms/0`.

>       "text": "1.0      General\n\n\n      1.1    Scope\n\n\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements of the Employer on Safety,\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor / sub-contractor and\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\n\n\n      1.2     Definition / languages\n\n\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual (EQM) forms an essential part of\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed by BMRCL  for  the\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\n\n\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS & ABBREVIATIONS\n\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including water, air\n                    and land and other living creatures.\n\n                b)      Environmental Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\n                       present in such concentration as may be or tend to be injurious to\n                      environment.\n\n                 c)      Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\n                      environmental pollutant.\n\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity that\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of the\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\n\n                e)      Monitoring is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\n                       provide information regarding the levels of pollutants released during\n                         construction.\n\n                       f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\n                      area within the limits of the work as shown on the Plans. Construction\n                            site  shall  also  include  staging, and  debris  disposal  areas  and\n                         transportation routes to and from these areas.\n                g)     Noise is any unwanted sound disturbance of the environment around\n                       the area of construction operations.\n\n                h)      Decibel is a measure on a logarithmic scale of the magnitude of a\n                          particular quantity (such as sound pressure, sound power) with respect\n                          to a standardized reference quantity.\n\n                           i)    A - weighted Noise levels in Decibels (referenced to 20 micro-\n                      Pascal) as measured with A-weighting network of standard\n                    sound level meter,\n                      abbreviated dB (A).\n\n                         j)      Energy Equivalent Level (Leq) is the level of a steady noise\n                     which has the same energy as the  fluctuating noise level\n                        integrated  over  the  period  of  measurement.  Lmax  is  the\n                 maximum Noise Level during the period of measurement. L10\n                   and L90 is the percentile exceeding levels of sound which is\n                    exceeded 10% and 90% of the time of measurement.\n\n                 k)     Waste  is  unwanted  surplus  substances  arising  from  the\n                         application of all construction operations and any substance or\n                            article which is required to be disposed."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 9,
>       "text": "l)     Suspended Particulate Matter is abbreviated as SPM and\n                           measured in µg/m3.\n\n                    m)     Environmental Quality Management Manual is abbreviated as\n                        EQM.\n\n                           n)     Air Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as AMCP.\n\n                          o)     Noise Monitoring and Control Plan is abbreviated as NMCP.\n\n                           q)      Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India is\n                                abbreviated as MOEF.\n\n                                   r)     Central Pollution Control Board, New Delhi is abbreviated as\n                        CPCB."

>       "text": "ii)   The use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended.\n\n                                     iii)   The use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered.\n\n                          iv)   ‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment.\n\n                      v)    Employer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC)\n\n                          vi)    Chief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall\n                         responsible for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document.\n\n                             vii)  BOCWA means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996\n\n                               viii)  BOCWR means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998\n\n                          ix)  DG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India.\n\n                      x)  BOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare\n                     Cess Act, 1996\n\n                          xi)  BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction workers welfare\n\n                    Cess rules 1998\n\n                             xii)   Building and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and\n                         Condition of service) Karnataka rules, 2006.\n\n                               xiii)  Notifications (Central and state) – collection of cess.\n\n\n          1.4      Application of this document\n\n\n          1.4.1     This document applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including\n                            all aspects conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be\n                no activity associated to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this\n                  document.\n\n\n          1.5     Purpose of this document\n\n\n          1.5.1    The objective of these guidelines is to ensure that adequate precautions are\n                   taken  to avoid  accidents, occupational  illness and harmful  effects on  the\n                  environment during construction.\n\n\n          1.5.2     This document:\n\n\n                                 i)    Describes the SHE interfaces between Employer and the Contractor.\n\n                                    ii)    Details the processes by which the contractor shall manage SHE issues\n                          while carrying out the work under the contract.\n\n                                     iii)   Describes by reference, the practices and procedures as given in the\n                BMRC  Project  Safety,  Health & Environment manual  for  best SHE\n                        performance.\n\n\n          1.5.3    These requirements shall be read together with BMRC Project SHE Manual,\n             OHSAS 18001-1999 Occupational Health and Safety Management System\n               and ISO 14001: 2004 Environmental Management Systems.  Definition of\n                key terms used in these requirements related to OHSAS 18001 and ISO\n                14001 standards are found in BMRC’s Project SHE Manual."

### J6e268122a6c15b66

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan|Clause 4.0 — Contractor SHE Policy and Plan]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "4.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 13,
>       "text": "4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\n\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display it at conspicuous places at work sites\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood by the majority of construction\n                   workers.\n\n\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\n                  submit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 14,
>       "text": "include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\n          following but not be restricted to:\n\n\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\n\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\n\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with  the  proposed\n                Contractor's agent;\n\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\n\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient information to\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\n                health and safety procedures;\n\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\n\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\n\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\n                including personal protective equipment;\n\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\n                condition and are operated in a safe manner;\n\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety plan;\n\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\n                 related matters, and\n\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure for reporting and investigating\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\n\n\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\n         Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\n           detailed, comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\n            site safety, industrial health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance with the agreed\n         procedures.\n\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\n          plan to the Employer for review.\n\n\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\n           industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\n          execution of the Work.\n\n\n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\n\n\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\n         No.: 3."
>     }

>       "text": "3.0      Compliance\n\n3.1     Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)\n\n\n3.1.1   A Memorandum of Understanding placed at Appendix No.: 1 shall be executed after\n          the award of contract before commencement of work by the contractor with regard to\n          various provisions on Safety, Health and Environment to be practiced during the\n          construction work.\n\n\n3.2     BMRC’s SHE Policy and Management Systems\n\n\n3.2.1    The construction works shall be undertaken in accordance with BMRC’s SHE Policy\n        and Management Systems as amended from time to time provided in Project SHE\n         Manual.\n\n\n3.3      Indian statutory requirements\n\n3.3.1     Primary statutory regulations\n\n\n3.3.1.1  Contractor shall develop thorough understanding about Building and Other\n        Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act\n        1996, Central Rules 1998, the building & other construction workers welfare cess\n        act 1996 and  central welfare rules 1998, Building and Other Construction\n       Workers [RE&C] Karnataka  Rules,  2006,  Building and Other Construction\n       Workers Welfare Cess act 1996 and Central Rules 1998, Notification [Central &\n         State] – Collection of Cess, not only to satisfy the Inspectors’ perspective but the\n       use  of  legislation  as  the  strong  tool  for  effective SHE management  at\n        construction worksites. Contractor is strongly advised to practice the principle\n         of voluntary compliance.\n\n\n 3.3.1.2 In order to facilitate the contractor for better understanding on the various provisions of\n         the above Act and Rules, a tabulated information highlighting the Sections/Rules\n          referring to the corresponding registration of contractors, maintenance of registers and\n         records, hours of work and wages, cess & welfare, medical  facilities and safety\n        requirements are given in Appendix No. 2. It is an indicative one and not a limiting list.\n\n\n3.3.2   In addition, the construction works shall be undertaken in accordance with all applicable\n         legislation and Indian statutory requirements listed below but not limiting to:\n\n\n                i)     Indian Electricity Act 2003 and Rules 1956\n\n                  ii)    National Building Code, 2005\n\n                  iii)    Factories Act, 1948, Delhi, Uttarpradesh, Haryana Factories Rules.\n\n             iv)   Motor Vehicles Act as amended in 1994 and The Central Motor Vehicles Rules,\n              1989.\n\n           v)    Indian Road Congress Code IRC: SP: 55-2001 ‘Guidelines on Safety In Road\n               Construction Zones.\n\n             vi)   The Petroleum Act, 1934 and Rules 1976\n\n              vii)  Gas Cylinder Rules, 2003\n\n               viii)   Indian Explosives Act. 1884, along with the Explosives substance Act 1908 and\n                the Explosives Rules 1983\n\n             ix)   The (Indian) Boilers Act, 1923\n\n           x)   The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and Rules 1991\n\n             xi)   Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and Rules 1950"

### Jf8809a71af85b566

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role|Clause 5.0 — Designer’s role]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "5.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 14,
>       "text": "5.0      Designer’s role\n\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "text": "5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\n                    affected by the work.\n\n\n          5.2      General philosophy\n\n\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\n                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\n                   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\n                a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\n                 However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\n                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\n                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\n                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\n                     or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\n                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\n\n\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\n\n\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\n\n\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);\n\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\n                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\n\n                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\n                           protect all people;\n\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\n\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\n\n\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\n               who have to use the design information.\n\n\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\n                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\n\n\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\n\n\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 16,
>       "text": "consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\n          designs.\n\n\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\n           sites even for short duration.\n\n\n5.7           If any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\n         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition"
>     }

>       "text": "                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": "                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": "          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": "                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": "                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": "                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": "                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": "                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": "                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": "                           protect all people;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": "                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses)."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": "          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": "          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": "                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "               who have to use the design information."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": "          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": "                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": "                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": "                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": "                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk."
>     },
>     {

>       "text": ""
>     },

>       "text": ""

>       "text": "          5.5      Employer’s approval"
>     },
>     {

>       "text": ""

>       "text": ""

### J9b89915bf84b73ea

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation|Clause 6.0 — Contractor SHE Organisation]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "6.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 16,
>       "text": "6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\n\n\n6.1      Education and Experience\n\n\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\n\n\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\n\n\n\n\n\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\n\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\n\n\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\n          procedural formalities.\n\n\n6.3      Approval from Employer\n\n\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\n           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\n          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\n\n\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\n\n\n6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\n        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\n        documents executed by the main contractor."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 17,
>       "text": "6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\n                  which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\n                      payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\n                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\n                          traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\n\n\n          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\n                    penalty clause.\n\n\n          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\n                   contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\n                      like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\n                  the cost of contractor.\n\n\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\n\n\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\n                  performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\n                    Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\n\n\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\n                    dispatch his duties effectively.\n\n\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements of such facilities / equipments to be provided\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003"
>     }

>       "pdf_page": 17,
>       "text": "7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\n\n\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate  in the making and monitoring  of\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment at their place of work. The\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees and Contractor and sub-\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase  the  involvement  and\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation and monitor the\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\n\n\n          7.2      Terms of Reference\n\n\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\n\n\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\n\n                                    ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure  its\n                        implementation\n\n                                     iii)   To review SHE training"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 18,
>       "text": "iv)   To review the contractor’s monthly SHE report.\n\n           v)   To identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in building or other\n                construction work and to suggest remedial measures.\n\n             vi)   To stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing\n                safety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing\n               posters or taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.\n\n              vii)  To go round the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and\n                detect unsafe  conditions and  to recommend remedial measures  for  their\n                  rectifications including first-aid medical and welfare facilities.\n\n               viii)  Committee team members should perform a  site inspection before every\n              committee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports.\n\n             ix)   To bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling\n             and maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other\n                construction work\n\n           x)   To suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site\n             and other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other\n                construction work.\n\n             xi)   To look into the health hazards associated with handling different types of\n                explosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest remedial\n             measures including personal protective equipment.\n\n              xii)  To review the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against\n               persons/sub-contractors for non-compliance if any.\n\n\n7.3       Within 14 days of award of contract, the SHE committee shall be constituted and\n           notification regarding the same shall be communicated to the members and employees\n         as per the format provided in Form No.: SF 001\n\n\n7.4       Site SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least once in a month with the\n        minimum members listed below:\n\n         Chairman           Project Manager\n\n           Secretary       SHE Manager (In-charge)\n        Members                     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\n                                                           ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\n                                                            iii)  In charge of site electrics\n                                           iv)  In charge of stores.\n                                    v)  Senior  Managers/  Engineers  heading   different  sub\n                                        functions.\n                                           vi)  Sub – contractor’s representative\n                                               vii) Labour Contractor’s representative\n                                                  viii) Workers’ representative\n                                           ix)  Co-contractor representative.\n                                    x)  SHE staffs\n          Employer’s\n                   BMRC SHE in charge and other representatives\n          Representatives\n\n\n 7.5    Construction SHE Committee meeting shall be conducted at least once in a week with the\n      minimum members listed below:\n\n    Chairman  Project Manager\n\n     Secretary  SHE Manager (In-charge)\n    Members     i)   Labour Welfare Officer\n                               ii)   In charge of plant and machinery\n                               iii)  In-charge of site electricity\n                      iv)  Senior Managers / Engineers heading different sub functions\n                   v)   Sub- Contractor’s representative\n                      vi)  Labour contractor’s representative\n                         vii)  Workers’ representatives\n                          viii)  All SHE Staffs"
>     },

>       "pdf_page": 19,
>       "text": "7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\n\n\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\n\n\n          7.6.2    The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\n                  value of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\n               workmen employed by each contractor in the contiguous area.\n\n\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE Committee meetings\n\n\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any two SHE monthly\n                  committee meetings.\n\n\n          7.8     Agenda\n\n\n          7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\n                 advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\n\n\n          7.8.2    The agenda should broadly cover the following:\n\n\n                                 i)     Confirmation of minutes\n\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance / condition\n\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\n\n                          iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\n\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\n\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’ SHE issues\n\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\n\n                               viii)  Report from Employer\n\n                          ix)   Matters arising\n\n                      x)   Any other business\n\n\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\n\n\n          7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\n                   No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\n                    followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\n                    the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\n\n\n          7.10     Disciplinary Action\n\n\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the meeting and\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other co/sub\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of monitory\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that the same\n                          is implemented."
>     }

### J766ce0d79cb7e9e8

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 8.0 — ID Card and First day at work, SHE orientation training|Clause 8.0 — ID Card and First day at work, SHE orientation training]]

> {

>   "fragments": [

>       "pdf_page": 19,
>       "text": "8.0      ID Card and First day at work, SHE orientation training\n\n\n          8.1     The Contractor shall ensure that all personnel working at the site receive an induction\n             SHE training explaining the nature of the work, the hazards that may be encountered\n                    during the site work and the particular hazards attached to their own function within"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 20,
>       "text": "the  operation. The  training  shall cover the contents as given  in the General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/004.\n\n\n8.2        All personnel shall be issued a photo identity card of size 85mm x 55mm duly\n        signed by the authorized representative of the contractor before they are\n        engaged for any work as per the format given in the General Instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/005\n\n\n8.3       Contractor shall also issue a personnel SHE handbook in a language known to the\n          workers, which provides information on SHE and emergency procedures that  all\n         personnel working on  contract are required  to know and the need  to  follow.\n          Contractor shall ensure that this  is distributed and  its content introduced to  all\n         personnel working at the site."
>     }

### J2d04a99a5037ea3a

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 9.0 — SHE Training|Clause 9.0 — SHE Training]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "9.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 20,
>       "text": "9.0     SHE Training\n\n\n9.1     The behaviour of people at all levels of the contractor is critical for SHE performance.\n\n\n9.2     The contractor shall organise quality SHE training to engage Managers, supervisors\n        and other personnel in behavioural change and improve safety performance.\n\n\n9.3     The Contractor shall analyse the training requirements for  all the employees and\n             initiate a  training program  to demonstrate  that  all persons employed,  including\n          subcontractors, are suitably qualified, competent and fit. This will include:\n\n\n                i)     Detailed Job  descriptions  for  all personnel,  to include  their  specific SHE\n                  responsibilities\n\n                  ii)    Specification of qualifications, competency and training requirements for  all\n               personnel\n\n                  iii)   Assessment and  recording  of  training needs  for  all  personnel,  including\n                subcontractors’ employees in the workforce, vendor representatives and site\n                   visitors\n\n             iv)   A system for assessing new hirers e.g. previous training\n\n           v)   A means of confirming that the system is effective\n\n             vi)   A matrix and schedule of training requirements, covering general, task–specific\n             and SHE-related training, showing the training frequency and interval between\n                refresher courses\n\n              vii)   Timely, competent delivery of training courses\n\n\n9.4     The contractor  shall arrange behavioural-based  training programmes  for  all the\n          executives to identify, recognise and eliminate unsafe act and unsafe conditions.\n\n\n9.5     The minimum Employer’s requirement of training needs for various categories of\n        employees are given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/006\n\n\n9.6     The contents of SHE training to Managers/Supervisors as given in general instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/007 shall be conducted.\n\n\n9.7     The refresher-training programme to all employees shall be conducted once in\n          six months.\n\n\n9.8      Toolbox talk as given in the Employer’s Project SHE manual shall be conducted\n          to all high-risk workmen everyday.\n\n\n9.9      On-the spot practical  skill development training on height safety including\n         scaffold safety, crane safety, welding safety, electrical safety, traffic safety for"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 21,
>       "text": "marshals shall also be conducted to all foremen/ workmen who were associated\n                   to the concerned jobs.\n\n\n          9.10     Every employee including workman shall take safety Oath daily without fail.\n\n\n          9.11      All vehicle drivers including heavy vehicle operators  shall be trained on\n                  defensive driving at Central Training Institute KSRTC, Shanthinagar Bangalore,\n                  or any other driving institute registered under Motor Vehicles Act.\n\n          9.12       All the above listed training programmes except at clause 9.11 shall be organised by\n                    the contractor only after taking approval from the Employer for the training faculty /\n                     organisation, content and durations.\n\n\n          9.13      In case of failure on the part of the contractor to provide  all the above-\n                mentioned training programs to  all employees in time, the same shall be\n                 provided by  the  Employer  through  accredited  agencies   if  required  by\n                  formulating a common scheme to all contractors. Any administrative expenses\n               and training fee towards the same shall be at the cost of the contractor."
>     }

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection|Clause 10.0 — SHE Inspection]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "10.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 21,
>       "text": "10.0    SHE Inspection\n\n\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting SHE inspections\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\n\n\n          10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\n                 and its supplementary procedures and programs.\n\n\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections program shall be adopted.\n\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\n\n                                    ii)    Routine Inspection\n\n                                     iii)    Specific Inspection\n\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1   Planned General Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined intervals and  it usually\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the Employer.\n\n\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee Inspection.\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\n                            contractors).\n\n                                     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\n\n\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment and\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\n                     structure erectors.\n\n                    Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and equipment by operator\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding supervisor\n\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools by competent electrical supervisor\n\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary electrical systems by competent electrical\n                          supervisor"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 22,
>       "text": "v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\n\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\n\n\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\n\n\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\n         developed procedures.\n\n\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\n          construction site:\n\n\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\n\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\n\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\n\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\n\n\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\n\n\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\n\n         Other inspections include the following:\n\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\n\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\n\n\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\n\n\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings."
>     }
